docs.text: MAR-40 Data Harmonization and Standardization Scope: Clinical and molecular cohort curation, data standardization, QC, and reproducible preprocessing for MAR-40. MAR-40 integrates heterogeneous immuno-oncology cohorts from University Health Network (UHN), University College London (UCL), and Université de Montréal / CHUM. This repository provides shared standards, documentation, and local Snakemake workflows for preparing standardized datasets. Nextflow is planned for downstream analyses across the broader MAR-40 research program; this repository does not claim those workflows are implemented here. The framework promotes FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) practices while keeping restricted patient-level data in approved environments. The Hwang example additionally uses a separately installed R/Bioconductor environment (tested with R 4.5.2); Pixi is not assumed to install those dependencies automatically. git clone https://github.com/bhklab/mar40-data-harmonization.git cd mar40-data-harmonization pixi install pixi run snakemake --version Example: clinical and RNA cohort pixi run snakemake --snakefile workflow/icb_hwang/Snakefile --cores 1 The Hwang (GSE136961) example has been run locally (21 matched clinical/RNA records; 381 annotated genes in the output MAE). Automated QC and broader cohort validation remain ongoing. See the Hwang example guide . Example: cohort characterization pixi run snakemake --snakefile workflow/visualization/Snakefile --cores 1 --dry-run pixi run snakemake --snakefile workflow/visualization/Snakefile --cores 1 The visualization workflow supports standardized cohort summary outputs and a synthetic example. See the visualization guide . docs.text: Clinical Metadata Standardization Status: MAR-40 harmonization guidance. Source-to-target mappings require cohort-level review; this is not a claim of full mCODE or ICGC-ARGO compliance. Standards alignment The MAR-40 clinical data dictionary is informed by selected common oncology data elements and definitions from mCODE and ICGC-ARGO . Adopt only variables that fit the available evidence and intended analyses. Retain source terms, transformation rules and mapping decisions. Domain Core information Critical validation Patient and sample cohort , patientid , sampleid , specimen relationships Keep patient-, specimen-, sample- and assay-level records separate Disease Primary cancer type, histology/subtype, stage, metastatic status Document ontology/taxonomy version; do not infer from study title Therapy Agents, PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 targets, combinations, therapy line, exposure dates Distinguish regimen from molecular target and from subsequent therapies Sampling Pre/on/post treatment, sample date/timepoint, tissue source Define time relative to an index exposure; preserve longitudinal records Response RECIST or study-defined response, R/NR mappings, assessment time Preserve original categories; derived binary outcomes must name criteria Outcomes OS/PFS time, event indicator, unit, time origin, censoring Validate event coding, time origin, handling of missing or competing data Access/provenance Access class, study ID, publication, source file/version No patient-level restricted data in GitHub Source-to-standard mapping checklist Register source file/version, population, assay and record granularity. Record the original field name, allowed values and study definition. Map to a MAR-40 target variable with documented rule and reason. Preserve unrecognized values as unresolved rather than inferring them. Review patient/sample relationships and longitudinal timepoints. Validate units, endpoint definitions, missingness, duplicates and mapping exceptions. Export standardized tables and a versioned QC/mapping report as permissions allow. Special considerations Response: Different trials may define response using RECIST, RANO, pathological response, or PFS-derived criteria. Do not treat these as interchangeable without a documented analysis-specific mapping. Survival: Preserve event and time origin; do not impose a universal follow-up censoring time as part of raw harmonization. Deduplication: Potential duplicates within and across institutional inventories need cohort/patient-level review. Site totals must not be summed as unique patients without linkage evidence. FAIR: Use stable identifiers, controlled terms, versioned mappings and access descriptors. FAIR does not require open release of restricted patient-level data.

docs.text: MAR-40 Data Curation and Harmonization SOP Version: 1.0 Scope: Participating MAR-40 teams curating clinical and molecular immuno-oncology cohorts Document owner(s): Farnoosh Abbas Aghababazadeh Related documents: Clinical metadata · Molecular standardization · Data dictionary · Data sources · Quality control · Usage 1. Purpose and expected outcome Establish a transparent, reproducible procedure for acquiring, curating, harmonizing, validating, and documenting clinical and molecular data contributed to MAR-40. Apply common data definitions across institutions while retaining the meaning and provenance of the original source records. At the end of curation, each cohort should have, where the source data permit : A versioned source inventory and provenance record. Harmonized patient- and/or sample-level clinical metadata with documented identifiers. Standardized treatment, disease, response, survival, and assay descriptors. Processed molecular data with documented units, reference annotations, and processing methods. An explicit linkage between clinical records and molecular samples; an MAE object when appropriate. A quality-control (QC) report, mapping log, unresolved-issues register, and reproducibility manifest. Principle: Do not invent missing clinical measurements, infer unsupported mappings, or silently discard records. An absent or unverified variable is not a negative observation. 2. Roles, accountability, and data stewardship Role Responsibility Contributing site / cohort curator Identify approved sources, perform source-level curation, record provenance and mapping decisions, run QC. Site scientific/data lead Review clinical meaning, data-access constraints, and flagged ambiguities; approve site-specific submissions. MAR-40 harmonization team Maintain shared schemas, mapping rules, versioned workflows, and cross-site comparability checks. Designated scientific reviewer Resolve decisions that change endpoint meaning, response definitions, tumor taxonomy, or assay comparability. Review rule: A curator must not independently resolve a clinically consequential ambiguity by guesswork. Record it as Needs review and escalate to the site's designated reviewer. Maintain a change log for decisions applied across cohorts. 2.1 Data protection and permitted sharing Classify data as Public , Controlled access , or Private , based on actual source permissions and institutional agreements. These labels describe access arrangements, not data completeness. Use only approved institutional environments for controlled/private patient-level information. Do not commit restricted source data, credentials, or direct identifiers to GitHub. Keep a shareable repository containing code, documentation, mappings permitted for distribution, test fixtures, and approved synthetic examples. Before sharing any outputs across borders or organizations, confirm the applicable ethics approval, data-transfer agreement, institutional policy, and export permissions. Technical reproducibility does not itself grant permission to share data. Where data cannot move between sites, execute the approved workflow locally and share only explicitly permitted metadata, reports, or aggregate results. 3. Overall workflow Register a cohort and verify access. Establish source, citation, scope, permissions, and local contact. Inventory source files. Preserve raw inputs; record file versions, assays, units, and identifiers. Curate clinical metadata. Standardize identifiers, demographics, disease, therapy, response, and survival fields. Process or import molecular profiles. Document RNA and DNA methods and preserve assay-specific information. Harmonize annotations and vocabularies. Apply versioned mappings for tumor types, drugs, endpoints, and features. Integrate sample-to-patient relationships. Produce interoperable tables and MAE components, when applicable. Perform automated QC and scientific review. Resolve or explicitly flag inconsistencies. Release curated outputs. Version outputs and record input provenance, code commit, software environment, and reviewer decisions. 4. Cohort registration and source inventory Create one entry per cohort in the registry described in Data sources . Record at least: Information Expected record Cohort identifier Stable project-specific cohort ID; avoid naming collisions across sites. Source Publication/DOI, accession, study documentation, provider, or approved local location. Site and curator Contributing organization, responsible curator, contact or team. Access status Public / Controlled access / Private, with permission or agreement reference. Study design Trial/observational; treatment arms and timepoints if documented. Data availability Clinical, RNA, SNV, CNA, other; raw vs processed; counts and formats. Source revision Download/release date, original filename, checksum where permitted. Use restrictions Distribution, reuse, location, and retention restrictions. Completion check: The origin and access status of every input file are traceable. Retain the original data as received; do not overwrite rawdata during standardization. 5. Clinical metadata curation 5.1 Define record granularity and identifiers Distinguish patient , specimen/sample , assay , treatment episode , and timepoint . Repeated samples from one patient must not be counted as distinct patients. Use site-appropriate pseudonymous identifiers and preserve an approved, protected linkage when necessary. patientid : stable within the defined cohort and uniquely linked to the relevant patient. sampleid : stable sample identifier; one patient can have multiple sample IDs. treatmentid : treatment regimen identifier when supported by the source. sample_timing : documented pretreatment/on-treatment/post-treatment or other timepoint classification; retain original dates/labels in controlled source records if permitted. When patient IDs can overlap between cohorts, identify a patient by cohort + patientid for summaries unless a verified cross-cohort identity linkage exists. Check: One molecular sample should resolve to an appropriate clinical patient record; any many-to-many or uncertain match requires documented review. Clinical variables must be evaluated at their appropriate observation level. Treatment, response, and sampling timepoint information may change within a patient; longitudinal differences should not automatically be classified as conflicting records. Confirm whether apparently inconsistent values reflect separate treatment episodes, samples, or assessment dates before flagging a patient-level conflict. 5.2 Required fields versus unavailable fields The MAR-40 target schema includes standardized fields such as patientid , treatmentid , response , tissueid , survival_time_os , survival_time_pfs , survival_unit , and the corresponding event indicators. Preserve these as the target schema where relevant; a cohort is not automatically ineligible because the source lacks a field. Domain MAR-40 target examples Key validation question Identifiers patientid , sampleid , treatmentid Are patient, sample, and therapy records distinguishable? Disease cancer_type , tissueid , histo , stage What exact disease classification and source terminology were used? Demographics age , sex Are units and coding documented? Therapy treatment , target Is the drug/regimen and treatment context supported by the source? Outcome recist , response Is the definition of response and assessment timepoint explicit? Survival survival_time_os , event_occurred_os , survival_time_pfs , event_occurred_pfs , survival_unit Are time origin, endpoint definition, censoring and units confirmed? Assays rna , rna_info , dna , dna_info Is assay availability distinguished from assay type and processing method? For the complete current target schema and accepted values, use Data dictionary . Do not treat the example field list here as a replacement for the version-controlled dictionary. 5.3 Harmonization decision procedure For each source column: Retain the source column name and original values in a source-to-target mapping record. Confirm the source definition from the publication, metadata file, protocol, or data provider. Select a target MAR-40 variable only where the meanings align. Specify the transformation (rename, recode, unit conversion, join, derived value, or no mapping). Record the decision status: Direct , Conditional , Needs review , or Unmapped . Document the reviewer, date, and evidence for clinical/biological interpretation changes. Re-run checks after updating a mapping rule; never edit only the final exported table. Suggested mapping-log fields: cohort , source_file , source_variable , source_definition , target_variable , rule_id , transformation , mapping_status , evidence , reviewer , review_date , notes . 5.4 Cancer taxonomy and disease annotations Map source disease labels to the agreed OncoTree version. Maintain Level 1 cancer type as the shared broad classification and Level 2 subtype when known and supported. Retain the unmodified original tumor label and the exact mapping code/version. Ambiguous histology, multiple primaries, metastatic specimen labels, or unsupported subtype assignments must be flagged rather than inferred. 5.5 Treatment and response Immunotherapy categories include: PD-1/PD-L1 , CTLA4 , IO+combo , IO+chemo , and IO+targeted . Preserve original regimen and component drug names; use agreed MAR-40 categories only after recording a documented mapping. Combination categories require an explicit precedence or multi-label rule agreed by participating teams. Keep RECIST best response ( CR , PR , SD , PD , or evaluability status when supported) separate from binary responder/non-responder outcome. Do not derive binary response from RECIST unless the study-specific response definition and threshold are documented. Record the assessment system/version and response timepoint when available. Stable disease and non-evaluable responses must not be assigned to a binary category without an explicitly documented, study-specific rule. 5.6 Survival endpoints Store OS and PFS times separately from their event indicators. Represent event values only after verifying the source's event/censoring convention (e.g. 1 = event, 0 = censored); never assume a coding direction. Use months for harmonized survival duration; preserve original units, the conversion method, and the agreed precision. Verify the time origin (diagnosis, treatment initiation, randomization, etc.). Do not pool survival measurements with incompatible or unknown origins without explicit analytical justification. Distinguish metadata availability (at least one nonmissing time or event field) from analysis readiness (a valid paired time/event record and a known endpoint definition). 5.7 Alignment with oncology metadata standards MAR-40 harmonizes relevant clinical metadata using selected concepts from mCODE and ICGC-ARGO , adapted into the MAR-40 research data dictionary. This is a mapping reference and does not establish full implementation or certification against either specification. For response, survival, treatment and specimen timepoints, preserve source meanings and document every transformation; see Clinical Metadata Standardization . 6. Molecular data curation 6.1 Inventory available assay data The curation workflow covers processed RNA-seq counts/TPM, microarray expression, RNA-seq FASTQ, SNV mutation files, and CNA segment or matrix data. For each assay record the originating platform, sample IDs, reference genome, gene annotation, pipeline/tool versions, normalization, filtering, and quality metrics where available. 6.2 RNA expression Prefer source-supported normalized expression values and record their measurement scale. An example expression transformation is log2(TPM + 1) . This is an assay-specific processing option, not a universal conversion rule: confirm applicability and document the pseudocount, normalization method, and whether the values were already transformed. If deriving TPM from counts, use documented feature lengths appropriate to the quantification level and record the source of lengths. Do not apply the illustrative conversion without validating gene-length definitions and the input's count type. For microarrays, retain the platform, probe-to-gene mapping, and source normalization information; do not label microarray values as TPM. 6.3 Mutation and copy-number data Record mutation type (SNV/indel), input format (e.g. VCF, MAF, gene-by-sample calls), variant-calling provenance, genome build, and filtering. Record CNA data representation (segments, copy-number calls, or gene-level matrix), reference genome and mapping methods. Where a binary gene-by-sample matrix is generated, preserve the logic converting raw calls to binary values and retain exclusions/uncertainties. 6.4 Annotation versions Use consistent gene annotations across datasets where scientifically appropriate, while preserving source provenance and compatibility with the reference genome: Source-reported annotations: Retain and document the original gene annotation and reference genome when known; do not relabel existing values as originating from another release. Standardized reprocessing: For datasets with accessible raw data, use the agreed MAR-40 reference genome and gene annotation release, with versions and processing parameters recorded. GENCODE v40 may be used where the approved workflow specifies a compatible GRCh38-based reference. Published/processed datasets with unknown annotations: Record the annotation as unknown until verified. Do not assume GENCODE v19 solely because raw data are unavailable. Assess compatibility before any conversion or integration; GENCODE v19 is a GRCh37/hg19-associated release and should be used only when justified by the source or agreed mapping procedure. Record the annotation release, reference genome, gene identifier format, and processing method for each dataset. Any conversion between annotation versions, gene identifiers, or genome builds must be explicitly documented and traceable, including the mapping strategy and any unmapped or duplicated features. Established gene, drug, and tumor annotation resources should be used consistently, with the corresponding resource versions recorded. 6.5 Molecular harmonization and reference implementations For detailed RNA expression scale/annotation handling, DNA SNV/CNA metadata, duplicate checks, and assay-specific QC, see Molecular Data Standardization . Snakemake is used for standardization/harmonization; Nextflow is planned for downstream MAR-40 analyses. The BHK Lab AnnotationGx and ICB_Common repositories can guide annotation and ICB processing; adopted functions and reference versions must be explicitly documented and pinned. Their inclusion here does not imply full integration or validation in MAR-40. 7. Build harmonized objects and link clinical/molecular data For R/Bioconductor workflows, supported integration objects include: SummarizedExperiment for expression or suitable feature-by-sample matrices. RangedSummarizedExperiment when genomic feature ranges are required. MultiAssayExperiment (MAE) to combine assays with clinical metadata and sample-to-patient links. Minimum structural checks: assay() feature/sample axes match rowData() and colData() ; each assay's sample IDs can be traced to the relevant patient; and sampleMap() relationships are checked rather than assumed. Maintain clear provenance when inputs differ by source, preprocessing or assay type. MAE should be considered a target integration representation , not a requirement to fabricate molecular assays for a clinical-only cohort. The exact MAR-40 output contract and filenames should be defined in Data dictionary and Usage . 8. Quality control and release gates Quality control (QC) is performed at three stages: source data , post-harmonization , and integrated outputs . Apply the checks relevant to each cohort and its available modalities; a clinical-only cohort does not require molecular-assay QC. Detailed validation rules, thresholds, and reporting conventions are maintained in the Quality Control Guide . QC stage Key checks Source data Verify file readability, source versions and provenance, expected identifiers, original coding, and permitted data access. Post-harmonization Validate canonical field names and permitted values; patient/sample uniqueness and linkage; supported disease, treatment, response, and survival mappings; missingness and unresolved decisions. Integrated outputs Confirm assay-to-sample/patient relationships, molecular feature identifiers, reference genome and annotation compatibility, assay dimensions and units, where applicable. Check generated outputs against input counts and documented transformations. Cross-cutting QC requirements: Record granularity: Assess duplicates and apparent conflicts at the correct patient, sample, treatment, or assessment level. Longitudinal changes are not automatically errors. Clinical interpretation: Verify response criteria, survival time origins, event/censoring codes, and derived variables before considering data analysis-ready. Completeness and provenance: Summarize missingness by cohort and relevant record level; retain source-to-target mapping decisions, exceptions, and applicable software/configuration versions. Issue tracking: Document each material discrepancy, its impact, resolution or outstanding status, and responsible reviewer. Do not silently impute missing values or discard records. 8.1 QC review and release decision Assign a documented disposition to each cohort or release: Pass: Applicable QC checks are satisfied, provenance is documented, and no material unresolved issues remain. Pass with documented limitations: Noncritical missingness or limitations remain, but their impact and permitted use are recorded and approved by the designated reviewer. Hold for review: Material clinical or molecular ambiguities, invalid patient/sample links, failed structural checks, or unresolved data-access concerns prevent release until reviewed. Record the QC disposition, reviewer, review date, outstanding issues, and any restrictions in the cohort QC summary. A Pass indicates completion of the specified curation checks, not automatic suitability for every downstream analysis. The Snakemake cohort visualization workflow provides descriptive QC support , including cohort summaries, variable-availability and missingness reports, and selected conflict flags. Its plots and tables do not replace source-level validation, scientific review, or endpoint-specific analysis-readiness checks. In particular, a nonmissing survival time or event field does not establish a valid time–event pair. 9. Outputs, reproducibility, and handoff Suggested cohort handoff contents, subject to institutional permissions: <cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Source inventory, versions, permitted paths/checksums ├── mapping_log.tsv # Source -> MAR-40 transformations and decisions ├── clinical_harmonized.csv # Approved de-identified clinical metadata, if shareable ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Available assays and processing parameters ├── qc_summary.tsv # QC checks, results, exceptions ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Items requiring reviewer decisions └── run_manifest.txt # Git commit, environment, execution parameters, date A molecular-data object (e.g. .rds MAE) may be produced in an approved destination when supported by the cohort and workflow. This is the recommended cohort handoff structure; include only files supported by the cohort and permitted by institutional access requirements. The implemented MAR-40 Snakemake visualization workflow can generate standardized descriptive figures, cohort summaries, variable-availability and missingness reports, and supporting QC tables from harmonized sample-level metadata. These outputs support curation review but do not replace source-level validation, endpoint assessment, or scientific approval. The suggested handoff files above are not all automatically generated by that workflow. Capture the following run details: source file versions/checksums, approved execution location, Git commit, Pixi/other environment lockfile, workflow command, tool versions, mapping version, start date, curator and reviewer. Scripts should be rerunnable without hard-coded local machine paths; use paths/configuration described in Usage . Suggested submission review checklist [ ] Data sources, access permissions, and provenance are documented. [ ] Clinical metadata follow the MAR-40 standardized data dictionary. [ ] Patient and sample identifiers are consistent and correctly linked. [ ] Cancer types, treatments, response, and survival variables are harmonized according to the agreed definitions. [ ] Molecular data processing, reference genomes, and source or approved target annotation versions are documented. [ ] Clinical and molecular data are correctly integrated, including MAE validation where applicable. [ ] Quality-control checks are completed, and unresolved issues are documented. [ ] Harmonized outputs and processing steps are reproducible using version-controlled scripts. 10. Handling exceptions and SOP changes When a source requires a deviation, document the affected cohort, reason, alternative procedure, scientific impact, decision owner and approval date. Reusable deviations should be proposed as a versioned SOP or harmonization-rule update via repository review. Retain prior mapping versions so existing outputs remain interpretable. 11. Maintaining cross-site consistency The harmonization framework is shared across participating MAR-40 teams. Each site should use the current version of the Data dictionary , Data sources , Quality control , and Usage documentation when producing a cohort release. Changes to shared variable definitions, OncoTree classifications, treatment grouping, clinical endpoints, assay representations, QC criteria, or output formats must be recorded in version-controlled documentation and reviewed by the designated scientific/data leads before being applied across cohorts. Site-specific exceptions remain traceable in the mapping log and QC report. Changes affecting the interpretation of previously harmonized cohorts should trigger an assessment of whether existing outputs require regeneration. Preserve the source definitions, transformation rules, and previous output versions to support reproducibility. --- Document history Version Date Status Summary 1.0 November 20, 2026 Active MAR-40 cross-site data curation and harmonization SOP for UCL, McGill University, and UHN; includes source provenance, clinical and molecular harmonization, QC, and reproducibility procedures.

docs.title: 2.1 Data protection and permitted sharing

docs.text: Register a cohort and verify access. Establish source, citation, scope, permissions, and local contact. Inventory source files. Preserve raw inputs; record file versions, assays, units, and identifiers. Curate clinical metadata. Standardize identifiers, demographics, disease, therapy, response, and survival fields. Process or import molecular profiles. Document RNA and DNA methods and preserve assay-specific information. Harmonize annotations and vocabularies. Apply versioned mappings for tumor types, drugs, endpoints, and features. Integrate sample-to-patient relationships. Produce interoperable tables and MAE components, when applicable. Perform automated QC and scientific review. Resolve or explicitly flag inconsistencies. Release curated outputs. Version outputs and record input provenance, code commit, software environment, and reviewer decisions.
docs.title: 3. Overall workflow

docs.text: Create one entry per cohort in the registry described in Data sources . Record at least: Information Expected record Cohort identifier Stable project-specific cohort ID; avoid naming collisions across sites. Source Publication/DOI, accession, study documentation, provider, or approved local location. Site and curator Contributing organization, responsible curator, contact or team. Access status Public / Controlled access / Private, with permission or agreement reference. Study design Trial/observational; treatment arms and timepoints if documented. Data availability Clinical, RNA, SNV, CNA, other; raw vs processed; counts and formats. Source revision Download/release date, original filename, checksum where permitted. Use restrictions Distribution, reuse, location, and retention restrictions. Completion check: The origin and access status of every input file are traceable. Retain the original data as received; do not overwrite rawdata during standardization.
docs.title: 4. Cohort registration and source inventory

docs.text: Distinguish patient , specimen/sample , assay , treatment episode , and timepoint . Repeated samples from one patient must not be counted as distinct patients. Use site-appropriate pseudonymous identifiers and preserve an approved, protected linkage when necessary. patientid : stable within the defined cohort and uniquely linked to the relevant patient. sampleid : stable sample identifier; one patient can have multiple sample IDs. treatmentid : treatment regimen identifier when supported by the source. sample_timing : documented pretreatment/on-treatment/post-treatment or other timepoint classification; retain original dates/labels in controlled source records if permitted. When patient IDs can overlap between cohorts, identify a patient by cohort + patientid for summaries unless a verified cross-cohort identity linkage exists. Check: One molecular sample should resolve to an appropriate clinical patient record; any many-to-many or uncertain match requires documented review. Clinical variables must be evaluated at their appropriate observation level. Treatment, response, and sampling timepoint information may change within a patient; longitudinal differences should not automatically be classified as conflicting records. Confirm whether apparently inconsistent values reflect separate treatment episodes, samples, or assessment dates before flagging a patient-level conflict.
docs.title: 5.1 Define record granularity and identifiers

docs.text: The MAR-40 target schema includes standardized fields such as patientid , treatmentid , response , tissueid , survival_time_os , survival_time_pfs , survival_unit , and the corresponding event indicators. Preserve these as the target schema where relevant; a cohort is not automatically ineligible because the source lacks a field. Domain MAR-40 target examples Key validation question Identifiers patientid , sampleid , treatmentid Are patient, sample, and therapy records distinguishable? Disease cancer_type , tissueid , histo , stage What exact disease classification and source terminology were used? Demographics age , sex Are units and coding documented? Therapy treatment , target Is the drug/regimen and treatment context supported by the source? Outcome recist , response Is the definition of response and assessment timepoint explicit? Survival survival_time_os , event_occurred_os , survival_time_pfs , event_occurred_pfs , survival_unit Are time origin, endpoint definition, censoring and units confirmed? Assays rna , rna_info , dna , dna_info Is assay availability distinguished from assay type and processing method? For the complete current target schema and accepted values, use Data dictionary . Do not treat the example field list here as a replacement for the version-controlled dictionary.
docs.title: 5.2 Required fields versus unavailable fields

docs.text: For each source column: Retain the source column name and original values in a source-to-target mapping record. Confirm the source definition from the publication, metadata file, protocol, or data provider. Select a target MAR-40 variable only where the meanings align. Specify the transformation (rename, recode, unit conversion, join, derived value, or no mapping). Record the decision status: Direct , Conditional , Needs review , or Unmapped . Document the reviewer, date, and evidence for clinical/biological interpretation changes. Re-run checks after updating a mapping rule; never edit only the final exported table. Suggested mapping-log fields: cohort , source_file , source_variable , source_definition , target_variable , rule_id , transformation , mapping_status , evidence , reviewer , review_date , notes .
docs.title: 5.3 Harmonization decision procedure

docs.text: Map source disease labels to the agreed OncoTree version. Maintain Level 1 cancer type as the shared broad classification and Level 2 subtype when known and supported. Retain the unmodified original tumor label and the exact mapping code/version. Ambiguous histology, multiple primaries, metastatic specimen labels, or unsupported subtype assignments must be flagged rather than inferred.
docs.title: 5.4 Cancer taxonomy and disease annotations

docs.text: Immunotherapy categories include: PD-1/PD-L1 , CTLA4 , IO+combo , IO+chemo , and IO+targeted . Preserve original regimen and component drug names; use agreed MAR-40 categories only after recording a documented mapping. Combination categories require an explicit precedence or multi-label rule agreed by participating teams. Keep RECIST best response ( CR , PR , SD , PD , or evaluability status when supported) separate from binary responder/non-responder outcome. Do not derive binary response from RECIST unless the study-specific response definition and threshold are documented. Record the assessment system/version and response timepoint when available. Stable disease and non-evaluable responses must not be assigned to a binary category without an explicitly documented, study-specific rule.
docs.title: 5.5 Treatment and response

docs.text: Store OS and PFS times separately from their event indicators. Represent event values only after verifying the source's event/censoring convention (e.g. 1 = event, 0 = censored); never assume a coding direction. Use months for harmonized survival duration; preserve original units, the conversion method, and the agreed precision. Verify the time origin (diagnosis, treatment initiation, randomization, etc.). Do not pool survival measurements with incompatible or unknown origins without explicit analytical justification. Distinguish metadata availability (at least one nonmissing time or event field) from analysis readiness (a valid paired time/event record and a known endpoint definition).
docs.title: 5.6 Survival endpoints

docs.text: MAR-40 harmonizes relevant clinical metadata using selected concepts from mCODE and ICGC-ARGO , adapted into the MAR-40 research data dictionary. This is a mapping reference and does not establish full implementation or certification against either specification. For response, survival, treatment and specimen timepoints, preserve source meanings and document every transformation; see Clinical Metadata Standardization .
docs.title: 5.7 Alignment with oncology metadata standards

docs.text: The curation workflow covers processed RNA-seq counts/TPM, microarray expression, RNA-seq FASTQ, SNV mutation files, and CNA segment or matrix data. For each assay record the originating platform, sample IDs, reference genome, gene annotation, pipeline/tool versions, normalization, filtering, and quality metrics where available.
docs.title: 6.1 Inventory available assay data

docs.text: Prefer source-supported normalized expression values and record their measurement scale. An example expression transformation is log2(TPM + 1) . This is an assay-specific processing option, not a universal conversion rule: confirm applicability and document the pseudocount, normalization method, and whether the values were already transformed. If deriving TPM from counts, use documented feature lengths appropriate to the quantification level and record the source of lengths. Do not apply the illustrative conversion without validating gene-length definitions and the input's count type. For microarrays, retain the platform, probe-to-gene mapping, and source normalization information; do not label microarray values as TPM.
docs.title: 6.2 RNA expression

docs.text: Record mutation type (SNV/indel), input format (e.g. VCF, MAF, gene-by-sample calls), variant-calling provenance, genome build, and filtering. Record CNA data representation (segments, copy-number calls, or gene-level matrix), reference genome and mapping methods. Where a binary gene-by-sample matrix is generated, preserve the logic converting raw calls to binary values and retain exclusions/uncertainties.
docs.title: 6.3 Mutation and copy-number data

docs.text: Use consistent gene annotations across datasets where scientifically appropriate, while preserving source provenance and compatibility with the reference genome: Source-reported annotations: Retain and document the original gene annotation and reference genome when known; do not relabel existing values as originating from another release. Standardized reprocessing: For datasets with accessible raw data, use the agreed MAR-40 reference genome and gene annotation release, with versions and processing parameters recorded. GENCODE v40 may be used where the approved workflow specifies a compatible GRCh38-based reference. Published/processed datasets with unknown annotations: Record the annotation as unknown until verified. Do not assume GENCODE v19 solely because raw data are unavailable. Assess compatibility before any conversion or integration; GENCODE v19 is a GRCh37/hg19-associated release and should be used only when justified by the source or agreed mapping procedure. Record the annotation release, reference genome, gene identifier format, and processing method for each dataset. Any conversion between annotation versions, gene identifiers, or genome builds must be explicitly documented and traceable, including the mapping strategy and any unmapped or duplicated features. Established gene, drug, and tumor annotation resources should be used consistently, with the corresponding resource versions recorded.
docs.title: 6.4 Annotation versions

docs.text: For detailed RNA expression scale/annotation handling, DNA SNV/CNA metadata, duplicate checks, and assay-specific QC, see Molecular Data Standardization . Snakemake is used for standardization/harmonization; Nextflow is planned for downstream MAR-40 analyses. The BHK Lab AnnotationGx and ICB_Common repositories can guide annotation and ICB processing; adopted functions and reference versions must be explicitly documented and pinned. Their inclusion here does not imply full integration or validation in MAR-40.
docs.title: 6.5 Molecular harmonization and reference implementations

docs.text: For R/Bioconductor workflows, supported integration objects include: SummarizedExperiment for expression or suitable feature-by-sample matrices. RangedSummarizedExperiment when genomic feature ranges are required. MultiAssayExperiment (MAE) to combine assays with clinical metadata and sample-to-patient links. Minimum structural checks: assay() feature/sample axes match rowData() and colData() ; each assay's sample IDs can be traced to the relevant patient; and sampleMap() relationships are checked rather than assumed. Maintain clear provenance when inputs differ by source, preprocessing or assay type. MAE should be considered a target integration representation , not a requirement to fabricate molecular assays for a clinical-only cohort. The exact MAR-40 output contract and filenames should be defined in Data dictionary and Usage .
docs.title: 7. Build harmonized objects and link clinical/molecular data

docs.text: Quality control (QC) is performed at three stages: source data , post-harmonization , and integrated outputs . Apply the checks relevant to each cohort and its available modalities; a clinical-only cohort does not require molecular-assay QC. Detailed validation rules, thresholds, and reporting conventions are maintained in the Quality Control Guide . QC stage Key checks Source data Verify file readability, source versions and provenance, expected identifiers, original coding, and permitted data access. Post-harmonization Validate canonical field names and permitted values; patient/sample uniqueness and linkage; supported disease, treatment, response, and survival mappings; missingness and unresolved decisions. Integrated outputs Confirm assay-to-sample/patient relationships, molecular feature identifiers, reference genome and annotation compatibility, assay dimensions and units, where applicable. Check generated outputs against input counts and documented transformations. Cross-cutting QC requirements: Record granularity: Assess duplicates and apparent conflicts at the correct patient, sample, treatment, or assessment level. Longitudinal changes are not automatically errors. Clinical interpretation: Verify response criteria, survival time origins, event/censoring codes, and derived variables before considering data analysis-ready. Completeness and provenance: Summarize missingness by cohort and relevant record level; retain source-to-target mapping decisions, exceptions, and applicable software/configuration versions. Issue tracking: Document each material discrepancy, its impact, resolution or outstanding status, and responsible reviewer. Do not silently impute missing values or discard records.
docs.title: 8. Quality control and release gates

docs.text: Assign a documented disposition to each cohort or release: Pass: Applicable QC checks are satisfied, provenance is documented, and no material unresolved issues remain. Pass with documented limitations: Noncritical missingness or limitations remain, but their impact and permitted use are recorded and approved by the designated reviewer. Hold for review: Material clinical or molecular ambiguities, invalid patient/sample links, failed structural checks, or unresolved data-access concerns prevent release until reviewed. Record the QC disposition, reviewer, review date, outstanding issues, and any restrictions in the cohort QC summary. A Pass indicates completion of the specified curation checks, not automatic suitability for every downstream analysis. The Snakemake cohort visualization workflow provides descriptive QC support , including cohort summaries, variable-availability and missingness reports, and selected conflict flags. Its plots and tables do not replace source-level validation, scientific review, or endpoint-specific analysis-readiness checks. In particular, a nonmissing survival time or event field does not establish a valid time–event pair.
docs.title: 8.1 QC review and release decision

docs.text: Suggested cohort handoff contents, subject to institutional permissions: <cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Source inventory, versions, permitted paths/checksums ├── mapping_log.tsv # Source -> MAR-40 transformations and decisions ├── clinical_harmonized.csv # Approved de-identified clinical metadata, if shareable ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Available assays and processing parameters ├── qc_summary.tsv # QC checks, results, exceptions ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Items requiring reviewer decisions └── run_manifest.txt # Git commit, environment, execution parameters, date A molecular-data object (e.g. .rds MAE) may be produced in an approved destination when supported by the cohort and workflow. This is the recommended cohort handoff structure; include only files supported by the cohort and permitted by institutional access requirements. The implemented MAR-40 Snakemake visualization workflow can generate standardized descriptive figures, cohort summaries, variable-availability and missingness reports, and supporting QC tables from harmonized sample-level metadata. These outputs support curation review but do not replace source-level validation, endpoint assessment, or scientific approval. The suggested handoff files above are not all automatically generated by that workflow. Capture the following run details: source file versions/checksums, approved execution location, Git commit, Pixi/other environment lockfile, workflow command, tool versions, mapping version, start date, curator and reviewer. Scripts should be rerunnable without hard-coded local machine paths; use paths/configuration described in Usage .
docs.title: 9. Outputs, reproducibility, and handoff

docs.text: [ ] Data sources, access permissions, and provenance are documented. [ ] Clinical metadata follow the MAR-40 standardized data dictionary. [ ] Patient and sample identifiers are consistent and correctly linked. [ ] Cancer types, treatments, response, and survival variables are harmonized according to the agreed definitions. [ ] Molecular data processing, reference genomes, and source or approved target annotation versions are documented. [ ] Clinical and molecular data are correctly integrated, including MAE validation where applicable. [ ] Quality-control checks are completed, and unresolved issues are documented. [ ] Harmonized outputs and processing steps are reproducible using version-controlled scripts.
docs.title: Suggested submission review checklist

docs.text: When a source requires a deviation, document the affected cohort, reason, alternative procedure, scientific impact, decision owner and approval date. Reusable deviations should be proposed as a versioned SOP or harmonization-rule update via repository review. Retain prior mapping versions so existing outputs remain interpretable.
docs.title: 10. Handling exceptions and SOP changes

docs.text: The harmonization framework is shared across participating MAR-40 teams. Each site should use the current version of the Data dictionary , Data sources , Quality control , and Usage documentation when producing a cohort release. Changes to shared variable definitions, OncoTree classifications, treatment grouping, clinical endpoints, assay representations, QC criteria, or output formats must be recorded in version-controlled documentation and reviewed by the designated scientific/data leads before being applied across cohorts. Site-specific exceptions remain traceable in the mapping log and QC report. Changes affecting the interpretation of previously harmonized cohorts should trigger an assessment of whether existing outputs require regeneration. Preserve the source definitions, transformation rules, and previous output versions to support reproducibility. ---
docs.title: 11. Maintaining cross-site consistency

docs.title: Document history

docs.text: MAR-40 Data Dictionary and Harmonization Guide Version: 1.0 Scope: Clinical, sample, treatment, outcome, and molecular metadata curated by MAR-40 teams at UHN, UCL, McGill, and other authorized collaborating sites Repository location: docs/data_dictionary.md Related documentation: Data Curation SOP · Data Sources · Quality Control · Usage 1. Purpose and principles This dictionary defines a focused MAR-40 research data model , not a conversion to OMOP. Its purpose is to support interpretable, reproducible harmonization of immuno-oncology datasets with different study designs, treatment regimens, response measures, and molecular assays. Map scientifically relevant variables , not every field in a source database. Use the same target field names across collaborating institutions, but do not assume fields with the same name have the same meaning . Each cohort must document original terminology, definitions, units, time origins, preprocessing, and any transformations. Preserve original records in their authorized storage environments; keep the harmonized version and mapping decisions traceable to those records. The common data model and overall approach are aligned with the MAR-40 SOP v1.0. Individual source-to-target mappings still require evidence-based curation ; values or conventions presented as examples below are not approvals to infer missing information. Key conventions Grain / level: The entity represented by each record (cohort, patient, sample, treatment episode, response assessment, assay). Do not flatten repeated visits, treatment courses, or samples without a documented aggregation rule. Requiredness: Identifier = required for records at the specified grain; Core = the harmonized column should be represented, but its value can be missing if unavailable; Conditional = required when that data type or analysis is present; Extended = enriches interpretation, where reported. Patient identity: Use (cohort, patientid) as the patient key unless a validated linkage shows that patients are identical across cohorts. Sample keys use (cohort, sampleid) . Missingness: Blank/ NA denotes an unobserved harmonized value. No or 0 is a negative value only if explicitly supported by the source , never a substitute for missing data. Capture the reason ( Not reported , Not assessed , Not applicable , Restricted , Unresolved ) in a supplemental missingness/issue log when known. Source fidelity: Retain the original source field/value, units, record level, and source evidence; avoid unsupported inference. Data governance: Schema, scripts, synthetic examples, and permitted aggregate summaries may reside in GitHub; controlled/private patient-level data must remain in authorized environments. 2. Recommended logical data structure Table or object Record grain Identifier / link Purpose Cohort registry One row per cohort cohort Source, permissions, modality coverage, dataset versions Clinical metadata One row per (cohort, patientid) or documented patient-treatment record cohort , patientid Baseline demographics, cancer characterization, outcomes Sample metadata One row per (cohort, sampleid) cohort , sampleid , patientid Specimen, sampling time, patient connection Treatment metadata One row per documented treatment episode cohort , patientid , treatmentid when available Regimen, components, targets, treatment setting Outcome assessments One row per documented assessment/episode Patient and treatment linkage plus assessment index/time RECIST/other outcome and assessment provenance Assay inventory / molecular objects One row per assay-sample combination, or appropriate MAE object cohort , sampleid , assay_id RNA/DNA modality, processing methods, features and measurements Mapping and QC logs One row per transformation, decision, or issue Cohort ID, source field, mapping rule/issue ID Auditability across sites A single sample-level flat CSV is an acceptable descriptive export if it maintains correct patient/sample links; it is not the canonical representation of longitudinal treatment, response, or molecular measurements. The visualization script may use such a flattened export. 3. Core clinical and sample variables Columns below are target MAR-40 names . String means a character value; identifiers should not be coerced to numbers (leading zeros may matter). Example categorical values indicate the expected format, not permission to guess a value. Domain Target field Level Requiredness Definition and permitted format Harmonization / validation guidance Identity cohort Cohort / all records Identifier Stable cohort ID; string Must match cohort registry; site-specific naming without collisions Identity patientid Patient and linked records Identifier Pseudonymous patient ID; string Unique within cohort; preserve cross-file linkage Identity sampleid Sample Identifier Unique sample ID; retain original terminology Disease histo Patient / tumor Extended Histology as reported; string Record histology system/code when available; keep provenance Disease stage Patient / assessment Core Source stage or valid harmonized stage; string Do not replace regimen with broad treatment class Treatment treatment_setting Treatment episode Extended Original and (when possible) standardized disease/treatment setting Preserve neoadjuvant, adjuvant, metastatic, etc. with evidence Sample sample_timing Sample Core Pre , On , Post , missing Relative to which treatment episode? Document source time and reference event; do not force ambiguous timepoints Sample sample_type Sample Extended Biological material (tumor tissue, plasma, PBMC, etc.) Record source material and collection method Sample sample_source Sample Conditional Primary , Metastatic , or original location/status if supported Preserve anatomical site separately; not interchangeable with timing Sample specimen_site Sample Extended Anatomic collection site, original/standardized Do not infer site from disease type Outcome recist Assessment / episode Core CR , PR , SD , PD , NE where criteria support them Confirm RECIST or other assessment system/version, assessor and timepoint; NE is not PD Outcome response Assessment / episode Core R , NR , missing Binary response requires source-supported definition ; do not automatically infer from recist Survival survival_time_os Patient / episode Core Numeric OS duration, months Confirm origin, endpoint and conversion from source units; nonnegative Survival event_occurred_pfs Patient / episode Core 1 event, 0 censored, missing Verify that original 0/1 meaning and endpoint definition align Survival survival_unit Cohort / outcome Conditional Original and/or harmonized duration units Harmonized durations use months; preserve original units and conversion rule Provenance data_source Cohort Conditional Accession, DOI, publication, or authorized internal reference Do not record credentials or restricted storage locations in public files Provenance access_type Cohort Core Public , Controlled access , Private Access status reflects permissions, not dataset quality; mixed status needs investigation or per-file classification Provenance source_version Cohort / file Conditional Release/date/checksum/version; string Required for reproducible provenance where available 3.1 Distinguishing clinical entities One patient may have multiple samples, sequencing assays, treatment regimens and response assessments. Patient-level response or stage summaries need an explicit aggregation/selection rule (for example, best overall response under a specified criteria and window); do not silently select a convenient record. If a longitudinal schema is not yet implemented, maintain companion tables or manifest entries describing the original grain and any aggregation applied to make a flat export. 4. Treatment and response definitions 4.1 Treatment classification The SOP recognizes the main MAR-40 immunotherapy groupings. Preserve at least three distinct concepts: source regimen , drug/immune target , and harmonized treatment group . Treatment group Interpretation Key caution PD-(L)1 PD-1 or PD-L1-directed therapy when classified as a single-target group Do not label a multi-agent regimen as monotherapy simply because it includes PD-(L)1 blockade CTLA4 CTLA-4-directed single-target therapy Preserve exact drug and mechanism IO+combo Immunotherapy combination not represented by a more specific selected category Specify which components qualify; avoid overlap with IO+chemo or IO+targeted IO+chemo Immunotherapy plus chemotherapy Confirm concurrent/combined therapy and study definition IO+targeted Immunotherapy plus targeted therapy Confirm exact combination and drug targets Other Documented regimen outside defined groups Preserve unmodified regimen Implementation note: A treatment classification must not rely on a substring match alone. Multi-component regimens require a versioned precedence rule or a structured multi-label representation. If a cohort does not supply the information needed, flag the classification for review. 4.2 Response recist and response are separate fields. For recist , document assessment criteria (RECIST v1.1, iRECIST or other), assessor, timepoint, and whether the result is best overall response . For response , record the cohort's responder definition and its relationship, if any, to RECIST. Clinical benefit, objective response, pathological response, and investigator-assessed response must not automatically be treated as equivalent . 4.3 Survival Use survival_time_os and survival_time_pfs in months, with original units and transformation documented. A verified event coding is 1 = event; 0 = censored ; if the source uses the reverse convention, document the recoding. Preserve time origin ( diagnosis , treatment start , randomization , etc.), event definition, and censoring rules in the cohort-level endpoint dictionary or mapping record. Availability of at least one OS/PFS field does not mean the cohort is ready for survival analysis ; each record requires a valid paired time/event measurement and a compatible endpoint definition. 5. Molecular variables and assay documentation Molecular metadata should distinguish assay presence , modality , measurement scale , and processing provenance . A Yes value is not an RNA-seq method; a No value must not represent unavailable information without evidence. Target field Level Requiredness Description and documentation rna Sample Core Availability status Yes , No , or missing; No only when explicitly assessed absent rna_info Sample / assay Conditional Source RNA technology/platform and processing description; use structured assay manifest for full details dna Sample Core Availability status Yes , No , or missing dna_info Sample / assay Conditional DNA modality (WES/WGS/panel/etc.) and processing summary assay_id Assay Conditional Identifier linking assay entry with sample assay_type Assay Conditional RNA-seq, microarray, WES, WGS, panel, SNV, CNA, etc. measurement_type Assay Conditional Counts, TPM, normalized microarray signal, variant calls, segments, gene-level CNA, etc. normalization Assay Conditional Algorithm, parameters, transformations and pseudocount (if any) reference_genome Assay Conditional Genome assembly, e.g. GRCh37/hg19 or GRCh38/hg38, verified from source/pipeline gencode_version RNA assay Conditional Verified GENCODE release; see §5.1 gene_id_type Assay Conditional Ensembl gene ID, gene symbol, probe ID, etc.; record version suffix policy annotation_version Assay Conditional Reference/annotation release, including non-GENCODE sources as applicable processing_pipeline Assay Conditional Tool/workflow name, version, reference and parameters processing_source Assay Conditional Published processed data, provided processed data, or MAR-40 raw-data reprocessing feature_mapping_version Assay Conditional Gene/probe mapping resource and release assay_qc_status Assay Conditional Pass / limitations / hold, as determined by QC procedure 5.1 GENCODE annotation strategy MAR-40 uses the following source-aware strategy : Published processed datasets: GENCODE v19 is the historical harmonization reference where applicable; however, do not assign v19 to a dataset solely because its true annotation is unknown . If the publication/provider specifies a different release, retain the documented release. If not verifiable, record Unknown in assay provenance and flag for review. Raw datasets available for standardized reprocessing: Prefer GENCODE v40 , with its compatible genome build and an explicitly documented quantification pipeline. Source-declared versions: When a publication or data provider identifies an annotation release, preserve that information even if it differs from v19 or v40. Record GENCODE release, genome build, gene ID type, quantification method, source reference and all conversions. Do not treat different GENCODE releases or builds as interchangeable , and do not label legacy expression measurements as reprocessed v40 unless actually reprocessed. 5.2 Multi-assay integration When appropriate, build SummarizedExperiment , RangedSummarizedExperiment , or MultiAssayExperiment objects. Validate feature and sample dimensions, rowData , colData , and the patient/sample relationships represented by sampleMap . A clinical-only cohort can be curated without generating a fictitious molecular assay. 6. Mapping rules and statuses MAR-40 mapping is key-variable, meaning-driven harmonization . It does not require OMOP concept IDs or conversion to OMOP database tables. Mapping status Definition Example / action Direct Equivalent meaning, grain, and units; rename or copy patient_id → patientid , after ID checks Conditional Meaning is compatible after verified recoding, transformation, or unit conversion Source OS_days → months with verified origin and conversion Needs review Source definition, endpoint, timepoint, or clinical equivalence is uncertain best_response → recist pending criteria check Unmapped No defensible target equivalence clinical_benefit must not be silently assigned response Recommended mapping-log columns: cohort , source_file , source_variable , source_value_or_code , source_definition , source_grain , source_unit , target_variable , target_value_or_code , transformation , rule_id , mapping_status , evidence , reviewer , review_date , mapping_version , notes . A mapping record may be variable-level (source column → target column) or value-level (source category → standardized category). Where a variable needs both, record both. Keep restricted source values in approved storage; public repository mapping examples should be synthetic or non-sensitive. 6.1 Illustrative mappings (not blanket approvals) Source field/value MAR-40 target Rule and necessary verification Status patient_id patientid Preserve as string; confirm cohort-scoped uniqueness Direct tumor_type = Skin melanoma cancer_type Map to OncoTree Level 1, record vocabulary release and original term Conditional best_overall_response = PR recist Confirm assessment criteria/version and definition Needs review until verified sex = Female sex = F Only after confirming source-recorded category Conditional OS_days survival_time_os Verify origin, censoring and unit conversion; do not copy numeric days into month field Conditional clinical_benefit = Yes response Not necessarily objective response; retain source meaning Unmapped pending scientific justification 6.2 OncoTree and tumor taxonomy Harmonize cancer_type to the agreed OncoTree Level 1 classification and populate cancer_subtype from Level 2 only when a supported mapping is available. Preserve the original histology/tumor label, code and OncoTree version. Distinguish tumor primary, specimen site and metastatic status; escalate ambiguous diagnoses or multiple primaries. 7. Quality control and completeness reporting Follow Quality Control and the SOP . At minimum, evaluate: QC area Core checks Identifiers Missing/duplicate patient or sample IDs, uniqueness in correct scope, patient-to-sample linkage Grain Patient-level variables repeated consistently; longitudinal assessments not inadvertently collapsed Allowed categories Valid treatment/access/response codes; list all unmapped source values Disease mapping Supported OncoTree Level 1/2, original labels and release preserved Outcomes Valid nonnegative times, verified event coding, paired time/event fields, time origin/censoring documented Molecular Assay availability vs type, gene IDs, reference build, annotation release, dimensions and sample mappings Missingness Report missingness by cohort, variable, patient/sample and, when relevant, timepoint Reproducibility Source versions, mapping log, code commit, environment, parameters, QC decisions Data access Cohort and source-file permissions, permitted destinations and sharing limitations Completeness ≠ comparability. For example, a cohort with a populated response column may still be incompatible with another cohort if response definitions differ. A heatmap cell of “Yes” signifies that at least one value was observed, not that all records are complete or analytically comparable. 8. Example export conventions and compatibility The current MAR-40 synthetic sample-level visualization workflow uses fields including cohort , patientid , sampleid , cancer_type , histo , stage , age , sex , treatment , target , sample_timing , recist , response , survival_time_os , event_occurred_os , survival_time_pfs , event_occurred_pfs , rna , and dna . docs.title: MAR-40 Data Dictionary and Harmonization Guide

docs.text: This dictionary defines a focused MAR-40 research data model , not a conversion to OMOP. Its purpose is to support interpretable, reproducible harmonization of immuno-oncology datasets with different study designs, treatment regimens, response measures, and molecular assays. Map scientifically relevant variables , not every field in a source database. Use the same target field names across collaborating institutions, but do not assume fields with the same name have the same meaning . Each cohort must document original terminology, definitions, units, time origins, preprocessing, and any transformations. Preserve original records in their authorized storage environments; keep the harmonized version and mapping decisions traceable to those records. The common data model and overall approach are aligned with the MAR-40 SOP v1.0. Individual source-to-target mappings still require evidence-based curation ; values or conventions presented as examples below are not approvals to infer missing information. Key conventions Grain / level: The entity represented by each record (cohort, patient, sample, treatment episode, response assessment, assay). Do not flatten repeated visits, treatment courses, or samples without a documented aggregation rule. Requiredness: Identifier = required for records at the specified grain; Core = the harmonized column should be represented, but its value can be missing if unavailable; Conditional = required when that data type or analysis is present; Extended = enriches interpretation, where reported. Patient identity: Use (cohort, patientid) as the patient key unless a validated linkage shows that patients are identical across cohorts. Sample keys use (cohort, sampleid) . Missingness: Blank/ NA denotes an unobserved harmonized value. No or 0 is a negative value only if explicitly supported by the source , never a substitute for missing data. Capture the reason ( Not reported , Not assessed , Not applicable , Restricted , Unresolved ) in a supplemental missingness/issue log when known. Source fidelity: Retain the original source field/value, units, record level, and source evidence; avoid unsupported inference. Data governance: Schema, scripts, synthetic examples, and permitted aggregate summaries may reside in GitHub; controlled/private patient-level data must remain in authorized environments.

docs.text: One patient may have multiple samples, sequencing assays, treatment regimens and response assessments. Patient-level response or stage summaries need an explicit aggregation/selection rule (for example, best overall response under a specified criteria and window); do not silently select a convenient record. If a longitudinal schema is not yet implemented, maintain companion tables or manifest entries describing the original grain and any aggregation applied to make a flat export.

docs.text: The SOP recognizes the main MAR-40 immunotherapy groupings. Preserve at least three distinct concepts: source regimen , drug/immune target , and harmonized treatment group . Treatment group Interpretation Key caution PD-(L)1 PD-1 or PD-L1-directed therapy when classified as a single-target group Do not label a multi-agent regimen as monotherapy simply because it includes PD-(L)1 blockade CTLA4 CTLA-4-directed single-target therapy Preserve exact drug and mechanism IO+combo Immunotherapy combination not represented by a more specific selected category Specify which components qualify; avoid overlap with IO+chemo or IO+targeted IO+chemo Immunotherapy plus chemotherapy Confirm concurrent/combined therapy and study definition IO+targeted Immunotherapy plus targeted therapy Confirm exact combination and drug targets Other Documented regimen outside defined groups Preserve unmodified regimen Implementation note: A treatment classification must not rely on a substring match alone. Multi-component regimens require a versioned precedence rule or a structured multi-label representation. If a cohort does not supply the information needed, flag the classification for review.

docs.text: recist and response are separate fields. For recist , document assessment criteria (RECIST v1.1, iRECIST or other), assessor, timepoint, and whether the result is best overall response . docs.text: MAR-40 uses the following source-aware strategy : Published processed datasets: GENCODE v19 is the historical harmonization reference where applicable; however, do not assign v19 to a dataset solely because its true annotation is unknown .
