docs.text: MAR-40 Data Sources and Cohort Registry Version: 1.0 Scope: MAR-40 participating teams at UHN, UCL, McGill University, and other authorized collaborating sites 1. Purpose and scope This document defines how contributing teams register and describe the clinical and molecular immuno-oncology cohorts used in MAR-40. It establishes a consistent cohort-level source inventory , not a common patient-level data model or an OMOP conversion requirement. The objectives are to: Provide an auditable description of each cohort's origin, scientific scope, and permitted use. Record whether clinical variables and molecular assays are available, and in what form. Capture annotation versions, processing methods, and sample/patient counts with clear definitions. Enable reproducible curation, harmonization, QC, and descriptive cohort summaries across sites. Support collaboration when patient-level or raw files must remain within approved institutional environments. The registry does not authorize transfer or release of data. Permissions are determined by ethics approvals, agreements, source licenses, and institutional policies. 2. Registry structure and record granularity Use config/cohort_registry_template.csv as the shared, machine-readable schema. Maintain the populated cohort registry in an approved location, with only explicitly authorized metadata committed to the repository. Register one row per cohort and source release . If an independently processed cohort release differs substantially in data content or provenance, register it as a separate version. Each row must have a unique registry_id . A cohort is a source-defined analysis population. It may contain multiple treatment arms, tumor types, molecular assays, patients, specimens, and sampling timepoints. Use companion manifests when these cannot be represented accurately by a single row: Source manifest: original files, hashes, locations, access conditions, and source releases. Assay manifest: one row per assay/data object with platform, sample coverage, reference versions, and preprocessing. Mapping log: source-variable-to-MAR-40 mappings, transformations, decisions, and unresolved issues. QC summary: executed checks, outcomes, reviewer decisions, and limitations. Do not combine patient, sample, specimen, or assay counts into a single field. Counts in the registry are descriptive and must specify their unit. 3. Cohort identification and provenance Registry field Description / recording rule registry_id Unique stable identifier for this cohort/release entry. cohort_id Stable MAR-40 cohort identifier; avoid collisions across sites. cohort_name Human-readable published or source name. contributing_site Site responsible for this registry entry (e.g., UHN, UCL, McGill). source_type Publication , Repository , Clinical study , Institutional , or Other . publication_doi DOI when available; otherwise leave blank. source_accession GEO/SRA/EGA/dbGaP or other source accession when applicable. source_reference Publication URL, data-provider reference, or descriptive source ID. Do not record restricted direct-access URLs or credentials in public files. study_design Interventional , Observational , Retrospective , Other , or Unknown as supported. source_release Original source release, dataset version, or documented snapshot. source_retrieval_date Retrieval or receipt date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) if applicable. curator Team/role or approved contact responsible for registration. last_reviewed Last scientific/technical review date ( YYYY-MM-DD ). registry_status Registered , In curation , Harmonized , QC reviewed , or On hold . This is workflow status, not data quality. Use Unknown (or blank where appropriate) when information is not established. Do not fabricate accession numbers, versions, publications, or collection dates. 4. Access classification and permissions Record the access classification based on actual source-level restrictions , not whether a team can currently view a file. Access type Definition Public The source is publicly accessible under stated terms; reuse restrictions may still apply. Controlled access Access requires authorization, a data access request, or contractual/ethics conditions. Private Locally or privately provided data not generally accessible through a public or controlled repository. Mixed Source components have different access classifications; resolve at file/assay level in the source manifest. Unknown Classification cannot yet be confirmed; flag for review. Store the registry fields access_type , access_reference , permitted_processing_location , cross_site_sharing_status , and restrictions_notes . For cross_site_sharing_status , use Permitted , Restricted , Not permitted , or Pending verification ; this is not inferred from access_type . Never commit patient-level restricted data, source credentials, identifiable information, or sensitive agreement details to the public repository. If a field is unsafe to share publicly, maintain it in an approved restricted site-local registry and publish only permitted metadata. 5. Cohort composition and clinical metadata availability Capture distinct counts separately: n_patients : unique individuals within the defined cohort/release. n_samples : unique biological sample identifiers; repeated specimens/timepoints may increase this relative to n_patients . n_assay_profiles : optional count of assay profiles/data columns, if verified. count_notes : data freeze, exclusions, partial-release coverage, or counting assumptions. Use Unknown or blank for unverified counts; zero means a verified count of zero . Capture source-supported characteristics without forcing a cohort into one category if multiple apply. When several categories are present, use a consistent, documented multi-value convention or companion table: Field Guidance cancer_types Source cancer types; mapping to OncoTree Level 1 is documented in the harmonization output. For multiple values, use a documented delimiter (e.g., semicolon) or a companion table; preserve original source labels. cancer_subtypes Source-supported subtypes or OncoTree Level 2 mappings; optional. treatment_regimens Source regimen labels or components; retain original drug names in approved source manifests. treatment_categories Harmonized categories when verified (e.g., PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA4, IO+combo, IO+chemo, IO+targeted). sampling_timepoints Pre , On , Post or source-specific terms, with ambiguity documented. clinical_age_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_sex_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_stage_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_response_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; specify endpoint type in notes. clinical_os_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_pfs_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_notes Relevant endpoint definitions, time origins, study restrictions, and caveats. Availability vs readiness: Yes indicates that relevant data have been identified, not that fields are sufficiently complete or comparable for pooled analysis. Readiness is assessed separately under Quality Control . Do not treat missing/unknown as No . 6. Molecular data inventory and annotations For each cohort, capture the following registry-level molecular metadata. These availability indicators summarize the cohort; the corresponding sample-level fields in the Data Dictionary are rna , rna_info , dna , and dna_info . Do not interpret missing or unverified data as No . Registry field Description / recording rule rna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; RNA data availability at cohort level. dna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; DNA data availability at cohort level. other_assays Other documented modalities, if present; do not infer absence from unreported assays. source_data_level Raw , Processed , Both , or Unknown . assay_notes Available assay types, source processing descriptions, coverage, and relevant limitations. For each assay, document in a separate assay manifest where applicable: Property Minimum documentation Assay identity Platform and assay type (RNA-seq, microarray, WES, WGS, SNV, CNA, etc.). Data representation Raw files, counts, TPM, normalized expression, segments, VCF/MAF, gene-level calls, etc. Linkage Assay sample identifier, biological sample identifier, cohort and patient relationship. Reference genome Assembly/build, when applicable (e.g., GRCh37/hg19 or GRCh38/hg38). Gene annotation Specific GENCODE version when known, or another documented source. Processing Pipeline name, version/commit, normalization, transformation, major parameters and QC results. Coverage Number of samples/profiles associated with the assay. 6.1 GENCODE strategy Document the project's working approach without retroactively assigning an unverified annotation to published data: GENCODE v19 is the principal reference used for applicable published/processed cohorts where harmonization follows the established published-data workflow. GENCODE v40 is the preferred annotation for cohorts with raw-data access that are reprocessed through the approved standardized workflow, when compatible with its reference genome and processing pipeline. Explicitly reported source version: retain and record the annotation release specified by the publication, data provider, or processing documentation. Undocumented source annotation: record Unknown until source evidence or identifier checks establish the actual release. Do not assert that published data used GENCODE v19 solely because it is a common project reference. Record gene identifier conversions, genome-build changes, and relevant compatibility limitations. A GENCODE release alone does not establish which reference genome or quantification method was used. Preserve the source-reported release and validate compatibility before applying an alternative reference. 7. Versioning, quality review, and maintenance Each registry record should be traceable to a source manifest or authorized provider record. When new data arrive: Update the source release and retrieval/receipt information without overwriting the original provenance. Recalculate and document counts from the appropriate grain (patient vs biological sample vs assay profile). Confirm data-access classification and reuse/sharing constraints. Reassess source field availability and molecular methods; record new or changed mappings. Re-run relevant QC checks and record whether outputs remain comparable with the previous release. Commit only permitted registry metadata and record the revision in version control. A change in annotation, cohort definition, endpoint meaning, or source scope must be documented rather than silently replacing a prior interpretation. Keep cohort-specific mapping/QC decisions outside the summary table when they require detailed evidence. 8. Using the machine-readable registry The config/cohort_registry_template.csv file defines a shared column layout. Copy it to an approved registry location and populate one row per cohort/release. The template contains no real cohort data . A populated registry may be shared through GitHub only when its entire contents are authorized for public release; otherwise, retain it in approved storage. The registry is intended to support source inventories and descriptive cohort summaries. It is not a substitute for patient-level clinical metadata, assay manifests, source-level permissions checks, or executable QC. For execution instructions, see Usage . For clinical target-variable definitions and source-to-target rules, see Data Dictionary . For validation and release checks, see Quality Control . Document history Version Date Status Summary 1.0 November 20, 2026 Active MAR-40 cohort source inventory and registry conventions, access classifications, clinical/molecular availability, provenance, and cross-site reproducibility.

Do not record restricted direct-access URLs or credentials in public files. study_design Interventional , Observational , Retrospective , Other , or Unknown as supported. source_release Original source release, dataset version, or documented snapshot. source_retrieval_date Retrieval or receipt date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) if applicable. curator Team/role or approved contact responsible for registration. last_reviewed Last scientific/technical review date ( YYYY-MM-DD ). registry_status Registered , In curation , Harmonized , QC reviewed , or On hold . This is workflow status, not data quality. Use Unknown (or blank where appropriate) when information is not established. Do not fabricate accession numbers, versions, publications, or collection dates.
docs.title: 3. Cohort identification and provenance

docs.text: Record the access classification based on actual source-level restrictions , not whether a team can currently view a file. Access type Definition Public The source is publicly accessible under stated terms; reuse restrictions may still apply. Controlled access Access requires authorization, a data access request, or contractual/ethics conditions. Private Locally or privately provided data not generally accessible through a public or controlled repository. Mixed Source components have different access classifications; resolve at file/assay level in the source manifest. Unknown Classification cannot yet be confirmed; flag for review. Store the registry fields access_type , access_reference , permitted_processing_location , cross_site_sharing_status , and restrictions_notes . For cross_site_sharing_status , use Permitted , Restricted , Not permitted , or Pending verification ; this is not inferred from access_type . Never commit patient-level restricted data, source credentials, identifiable information, or sensitive agreement details to the public repository. If a field is unsafe to share publicly, maintain it in an approved restricted site-local registry and publish only permitted metadata.
docs.title: 4. Access classification and permissions

docs.text: Capture distinct counts separately: n_patients : unique individuals within the defined cohort/release. n_samples : unique biological sample identifiers; repeated specimens/timepoints may increase this relative to n_patients . n_assay_profiles : optional count of assay profiles/data columns, if verified. count_notes : data freeze, exclusions, partial-release coverage, or counting assumptions. Use Unknown or blank for unverified counts; zero means a verified count of zero . Capture source-supported characteristics without forcing a cohort into one category if multiple apply. When several categories are present, use a consistent, documented multi-value convention or companion table: Field Guidance cancer_types Source cancer types; mapping to OncoTree Level 1 is documented in the harmonization output. For multiple values, use a documented delimiter (e.g., semicolon) or a companion table; preserve original source labels. cancer_subtypes Source-supported subtypes or OncoTree Level 2 mappings; optional. treatment_regimens Source regimen labels or components; retain original drug names in approved source manifests. treatment_categories Harmonized categories when verified (e.g., PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA4, IO+combo, IO+chemo, IO+targeted). sampling_timepoints Pre , On , Post or source-specific terms, with ambiguity documented. clinical_age_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_sex_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_stage_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_response_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; specify endpoint type in notes. clinical_os_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_pfs_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_notes Relevant endpoint definitions, time origins, study restrictions, and caveats. Availability vs readiness: Yes indicates that relevant data have been identified, not that fields are sufficiently complete or comparable for pooled analysis. Readiness is assessed separately under Quality Control . Do not treat missing/unknown as No .
docs.title: 5. Cohort composition and clinical metadata availability

docs.text: For each cohort, capture the following registry-level molecular metadata. These availability indicators summarize the cohort; the corresponding sample-level fields in the Data Dictionary are rna , rna_info , dna , and dna_info . Do not interpret missing or unverified data as No . Registry field Description / recording rule rna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; RNA data availability at cohort level. dna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; DNA data availability at cohort level. other_assays Other documented modalities, if present; do not infer absence from unreported assays. source_data_level Raw , Processed , Both , or Unknown . assay_notes Available assay types, source processing descriptions, coverage, and relevant limitations. For each assay, document in a separate assay manifest where applicable: Property Minimum documentation Assay identity Platform and assay type (RNA-seq, microarray, WES, WGS, SNV, CNA, etc.). Data representation Raw files, counts, TPM, normalized expression, segments, VCF/MAF, gene-level calls, etc. Linkage Assay sample identifier, biological sample identifier, cohort and patient relationship. Reference genome Assembly/build, when applicable (e.g., GRCh37/hg19 or GRCh38/hg38). Gene annotation Specific GENCODE version when known, or another documented source. Processing Pipeline name, version/commit, normalization, transformation, major parameters and QC results. Coverage Number of samples/profiles associated with the assay.
docs.title: 6. Molecular data inventory and annotations

docs.text: Document the project's working approach without retroactively assigning an unverified annotation to published data: GENCODE v19 is the principal reference used for applicable published/processed cohorts where harmonization follows the established published-data workflow. GENCODE v40 is the preferred annotation for cohorts with raw-data access that are reprocessed through the approved standardized workflow, when compatible with its reference genome and processing pipeline. Explicitly reported source version: retain and record the annotation release specified by the publication, data provider, or processing documentation. Undocumented source annotation: record Unknown until source evidence or identifier checks establish the actual release. Do not assert that published data used GENCODE v19 solely because it is a common project reference. Record gene identifier conversions, genome-build changes, and relevant compatibility limitations. A GENCODE release alone does not establish which reference genome or quantification method was used. Preserve the source-reported release and validate compatibility before applying an alternative reference.
docs.title: 6.1 GENCODE strategy

docs.text: Each registry record should be traceable to a source manifest or authorized provider record. When new data arrive: Update the source release and retrieval/receipt information without overwriting the original provenance. Recalculate and document counts from the appropriate grain (patient vs biological sample vs assay profile). Confirm data-access classification and reuse/sharing constraints. Reassess source field availability and molecular methods; record new or changed mappings. Re-run relevant QC checks and record whether outputs remain comparable with the previous release. Commit only permitted registry metadata and record the revision in version control. A change in annotation, cohort definition, endpoint meaning, or source scope must be documented rather than silently replacing a prior interpretation. Keep cohort-specific mapping/QC decisions outside the summary table when they require detailed evidence.
docs.title: 7. Versioning, quality review, and maintenance

docs.text: The config/cohort_registry_template.csv file defines a shared column layout. Copy it to an approved registry location and populate one row per cohort/release. The template contains no real cohort data . A populated registry may be shared through GitHub only when its entire contents are authorized for public release; otherwise, retain it in approved storage. The registry is intended to support source inventories and descriptive cohort summaries. It is not a substitute for patient-level clinical metadata, assay manifests, source-level permissions checks, or executable QC. For execution instructions, see Usage . For clinical target-variable definitions and source-to-target rules, see Data Dictionary . For validation and release checks, see Quality Control .

docs.text: Example 1 — ICB_Hwang (Clinical + RNA) Status: Implemented and successfully executed locally using Pixi, Snakemake, and R. Automated quality control is planned. Overview The Hwang immunotherapy cohort is available through GEO accession GSE136961 . This example demonstrates a reproducible workflow for harmonizing clinical metadata and targeted RNA expression data and integrating them into an expression-only MultiAssayExperiment (MAE). The workflow uses GEO clinical metadata, TPM-normalized gene expression, cohort-specific clinical harmonization functions, and GENCODE v19 gene annotations. It does not generate DNA assay data. Component Validated local result Clinical records 21 RNA expression samples 21 Original expression features 393 Harmonized expression genes 390 Genes matched to GENCODE v19 381 Unmatched genes 9 Annotated genes 381 MAE sample mappings 21 Expression transformation log2(TPM + 1) Gene annotation GENCODE v19 The expression data originate from an Oncomine Immune Response Research Assay targeted immune-response panel, not whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing. Source and attribution Original repository: RibaA/ICB_Hwang GEO dataset: GSE136961 MAR-40 R scripts: workflow/icb_hwang/scripts/ Snakemake entry point: workflow/icb_hwang/Snakefile Rule definitions: workflow/icb_hwang/rules.smk Configuration: config/icb_hwang.yaml The MAR-40 implementation adapts the original Hwang processing scripts to this repository's paths and Snakemake orchestration, while preserving cohort-specific processing conventions where applicable. Repository structure config/ └── icb_hwang.yaml workflow/ └── icb_hwang/ ├── Snakefile ├── rules.smk └── scripts/ ├── format_downloaded_data.R ├── Format_CLIN.R ├── Format_cased_sequenced.R ├── Format_EXPR.R └── create_MAE.R data/ └── examples/ └── icb_hwang/ ├── README.md ├── download/ ├── annot/ └── curation/ The Hwang workflow has a dedicated Snakefile and runs independently of the clinical visualization workflow. Required local input data Place the following files under data/examples/icb_hwang/ before running the workflow. Directory Required file Purpose download/ GSE136961_series_matrix.txt.gz GEO sample and clinical metadata download/ GSE136961_TPM.tsv.gz TPM-normalized targeted expression annot/ curation_tissue.csv Tissue harmonization annot/ Gencode.v19.annotation.RData Gene annotations ( features_gene ) Other provenance files, such as curation_drug.csv and DATASET_LOAD_INFO.csv , may be retained locally in annot/ ; they are not declared as required inputs in the current five-rule pipeline. The current Snakemake workflow expects these input files locally ; it does not download them automatically. Local downloads, annotation binaries, and generated curation files are excluded from Git unless separately approved for redistribution. Processing workflow The workflow consists of five R scripts, with execution and dependencies managed by Snakemake. Step R script Output under curation/ 1. GEO preprocessing format_downloaded_data.R CLIN.txt , EXP_TPM.tsv 2. Clinical harmonization Format_CLIN.R CLIN.csv 3. Molecular availability Format_cased_sequenced.R cased_sequenced.csv 4. RNA harmonization Format_EXPR.R EXPR.csv 5. MAE construction create_MAE.R ICB_Hwang.rds GEO preprocessing and sample mapping format_downloaded_data.R extracts sample metadata from the GEO series matrix and reads the compressed TPM data through an R gzip connection. Expression columns identified by sample titles (for example, D01 , D06 , and N10 ) are matched against clin$title and renamed using the corresponding clin$geo_accession values ( GSM... ). Original downloaded files remain unchanged. Clinical harmonization Format_CLIN.R preserves the original GEO metadata fields and creates legacy ICB clinical variables, including tissue classification, treatment class, survival times, event indicators, and derived response annotations. Survival times are converted from days to months. The cohort included nivolumab or pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1); the study-level treatment options should not be interpreted as verified patient-specific combined therapy. Get_Response() may derive response using PFS-related information rather than directly reproducing the source study's RECIST-based durable clinical benefit classification. These definitions require scientific review for cross-cohort analyses. Molecular availability Format_cased_sequenced.R creates the legacy ICB fields patient , snv , cna , and expr . RNA availability is checked against expression sample columns. SNV/CNA data not supplied in this curated example should not be interpreted as biological absence of alterations. RNA expression harmonization Format_EXPR.R extracts gene symbols from Symbol_ID , resolves duplicate symbols by retaining the row with the highest total TPM across samples, and keeps RNA-available samples. Values are transformed using log2(TPM + 1) . The output matrix has genes as rows and GEO GSM sample identifiers as columns. MultiAssayExperiment construction create_MAE.R joins harmonized clinical and expression samples by matching identifiers, annotates genes using GENCODE v19, and constructs an expression-only MAE with a ranged SummarizedExperiment. Genes without matching annotation are omitted from the annotated MAE but remain in EXPR.csv . Software dependencies Pixi: Launches the workflow tooling. Snakemake: Schedules and connects the five processing rules. R: Performs scientific data processing and constructs the MAE. The successfully tested local installation used R 4.5.2 on Windows . The R dependencies checked successfully were GEOquery , Biobase , data.table , stringr , tibble , SummarizedExperiment , MultiAssayExperiment , GenomicRanges , and S4Vectors . Format_CLIN.R currently loads shared functions from ICB_Common on GitHub using source() . This requires internet access at execution time and does not yet pin those remote functions to a specific commit. The Pixi environment should not be assumed to manage the separately installed Windows R packages unless explicitly configured to do so. The R executable is configured through config/icb_hwang.yaml . The workflow was successfully tested using R 4.5.2 on Windows ( C:/Program Files/R/R-4.5.2/bin/x64/Rscript.exe ). Users should update this path for their local installation. Run from the repository root Commands below use Git Bash syntax: # Inspect registered rules pixi run snakemake \ --snakefile workflow/icb_hwang/Snakefile \ --list-rules # Preview dependencies; does not run R pixi run snakemake \ --snakefile workflow/icb_hwang/Snakefile \ --cores 1 \ --dry-run # Execute the Hwang workflow pixi run snakemake \ --snakefile workflow/icb_hwang/Snakefile \ --cores 1 \ --printshellcmds In PowerShell, run each command on one line or use PowerShell's backtick continuation instead of \ . The final object is saved to: data/examples/icb_hwang/curation/ICB_Hwang.rds Validated local execution In the successful local run, 393 original expression features were reduced to 390 harmonized genes ; 381 genes matched GENCODE v19 and 9 were unmatched . The final MAE contained 381 annotated gene rows and 21 expression columns . The MAE contained 21 clinical records and its sampleMap had 21 mappings , with matching GEO GSM identifiers for primary and assay colname . These are observed local results showing successful processing and technical clinical–RNA sample integration. They do not establish that every clinical harmonization field has undergone full scientific validation. For manual inspection in R: library(MultiAssayExperiment) mae <- readRDS("data/examples/icb_hwang/curation/ICB_Hwang.rds") dim(mae[["expr"]]) nrow(colData(mae)) sampleMap(mae) Quality control and planned improvements Automated QC is deferred. Initial manual inspection confirmed that expression samples and clinical records were present and linked in the MAE. Planned additions include automated sample correspondence checks, missingness and identifier validation, response/survival definition review, gene mapping summaries, source checksums, pinned ICB_Common functions, and cross-platform environment testing. MAR-40 data dictionary considerations This example retains some legacy ICB field definitions for compatibility with the original workflow. In particular, the meanings of rna and rna_info and the use of GSM accession as the legacy patient key differ from the MAR-40 core metadata specification. Future use in standardized MAR-40 visualizations or cross-cohort analyses should employ a documented mapping or adapter rather than silently changing the cohort-specific source fields. Data sharing Only scripts, configurations, documentation, and approved example resources should be committed to Git. Original downloaded inputs, large annotations, generated harmonized matrices, and MAE objects should remain local unless their sharing is explicitly reviewed and permitted. The documentation alone does not provide all source files or make the workflow completely self-contained.

docs.text: Molecular Data Standardization and Annotation Status: MAR-40 working conventions and recommended checks. Local Hwang clinical/RNA processing is technically demonstrated; broader cohort-level RNA and DNA QC and cross-site validation are ongoing. Scope and responsibilities Use Snakemake for curation, preprocessing, standardization, and harmonization of clinical/molecular datasets. UHN coordinates the RNA-focused workflows and UCL coordinates the DNA-focused workflows, while both institutional inventories may contain multiple assay types. Nextflow is the planned framework for downstream analyses throughout MAR-40 , and should not be represented here as an implemented standardization pipeline. Per-cohort molecular manifest For every assay record: cohort, patient and sample identifiers, specimen/timepoint, assay type (RNA-seq/WTS, targeted RNA, microarray, SNV/indel, CNA, WES/WGS, etc.), raw/processed availability, source file/version, genome build, annotation release, normalization/transform, units, software versions, QC status and access restrictions. RNA expression processing and harmonization Record whether input is FASTQ, counts, TPM, FPKM, log-scale expression, microarray or targeted panel. Never label different measurement scales as equivalent. For raw RNA-seq, document reference genome/transcriptome, quantification method, feature lengths and import to gene level; retain the pipeline and annotation versions. Salmon/tximport may be used only if selected and validated for that cohort . For processed profiles, preserve the original assay scale and transformation; log2(TPM + 1) is a possible analysis representation, not a universal default . Harmonize gene identifiers using an agreed species/build/annotation release; preserve source IDs and a mapping audit (unmapped, ambiguous, duplicate identifiers). Do not assume all data share the same GENCODE version. Preserve assay platform distinctions (bulk RNA-seq, NanoString, microarray); record probe-to-gene mappings and platform-specific preprocessing. Match expression samples to clinical metadata using validated cohort/patient/sample keys; keep multiple timepoints/aliquots distinct. Record sample-level QC and feature filtering per cohort , without silently imposing an external study's expression threshold. DNA processing and harmonization Document DNA assay scope (panel/WES/WGS), reference build, callable territory, variant caller, filters and originating format (VCF/MAF/gene matrix). Standardize gene and variant annotations with genome-build-aware mappings; preserve mutation consequences, raw calls, and provenance. Keep SNV/indel and copy-number representations distinct; document rules for deriving gene-level or binary alteration matrices. Record whether TMB is source-reported or derived, whether synonymous variants are excluded, assay territory and callable denominator; TMB comparisons require consistent measurement definitions. Document sample purity, coverage, tumor-normal status and assay-specific QC when available; mark unavailable QC honestly. Identify potential within-cohort and cross-cohort duplicates for scientific review; thresholds from earlier papers are references , not automatically MAR-40 QC policy. Annotation tools and reusable lab code AnnotationGx : BHK Lab resource for constructing/querying annotations. Assess the current interface and relevant reference sources before introducing it into MAR-40; pin a version or commit and record database releases and mapping outcomes. ICB_Common : Shared scripts/conventions that can inform immune-checkpoint-blockade cohort formatting and annotations. Document which functions are imported, exact commit, inputs and outputs; avoid downloading unpinned code at runtime. GENCODE/HGNC/Ensembl or other reference sources: Document reference genome, release and identifier crosswalk before applying any conversion. Do not assume feature identifiers from different releases are directly interchangeable. docs.text: MAR-40 Quality Control Framework Version: 1.0 Scope: Clinical, sample, treatment, outcome, and molecular data curated by MAR-40 collaborating teams at UHN, UCL, McGill, and other authorized sites Repository location: docs/quality_control.md Related documents: Data Curation SOP · Data Dictionary · Data Sources · Usage 1. Purpose and guiding principles This document establishes consistent, traceable quality-control (QC) procedures for MAR-40 cohort curation and harmonization. Participating sites apply the same validation concepts and reporting conventions while processing restricted datasets inside authorized environments. The framework is variable- and analysis-oriented ; conversion to OMOP is not required. The goal is to distinguish three questions: Is the source documented? Can the source, access permissions, file versions, record grain, and relevant clinical/molecular definitions be verified? Is the harmonization correct? Are identifiers, values, units, transformations, annotation releases, and sample links consistent with the Data Dictionary ? Is the result fit for its intended analysis? Are necessary values and endpoint/assay definitions sufficiently complete and comparable for the specific analysis being considered? Guiding principles Preserve source records in approved storage; never overwrite original values during harmonization. Do not convert NA , Unknown , or an absent assessment into No , 0 , non-response, or a censored event. Do not resolve clinical or biological ambiguity by guessing. Record evidence and flag unresolved cases. Assess QC at the correct record grain (cohort, patient, sample, treatment episode, response assessment, or assay). Report counts and denominators . Distinguish samples from unique cohort-patients. QC status describes the readiness of a particular output for a declared purpose , not a blanket judgment of cohort quality. Keep local, restricted row-level issue files separate from shareable summaries; release only what data permissions allow. 2. QC stages and responsibilities Stage Input Main checks Output A. Source QC Original source tables, files, publication/provider documentation Provenance, permissions, file integrity, source schema, identifiers, assay definitions Source manifest and source QC findings B. Post-harmonization QC Standardized clinical/sample/treatment tables and mapping log Target schema, transformations, controlled values, missingness, consistency, endpoint definitions Clinical QC and mapping-issue summaries C. Integration QC Molecular assay files, sample mappings, optional SE/MAE objects Sample linkage, feature IDs, annotation/build, matrix dimensions, assay provenance Molecular/integration QC summary D. Release review QC results, issues, manifests, outputs Outstanding blocking findings, documented limitations, authorized destination Cohort QC disposition and reviewer record Responsibilities: The contributing site's curator executes and documents checks. Site scientific/data leads review clinically important ambiguities and access restrictions. The MAR-40 harmonization team maintains shared rules and evaluates cross-cohort comparability. Changes to the shared rules follow the SOP's version-control process. 3. QC finding severity and cohort dispositions Finding severity and cohort disposition are different fields and must not be conflated. Finding severity Meaning Typical action Error Violates a required integrity, identity, security, or validated data-contract rule Correct or place the affected output on hold Review Scientific meaning, mapping, compatibility, or linkage is ambiguous Investigate; document interpretation and reviewer decision Info Expected missingness, study limitation, or nonblocking deviation Quantify and disclose; retain for analysis planning The final cohort/output disposition is one of: Pass: Applicable checks completed without unresolved blocking findings; essential provenance is available. Pass with documented limitations: Data are usable for a stated purpose but have nonblocking limitations that are recorded and reviewed. Hold for review: Blocking integrity/access problems or material unresolved mapping/endpoint/assay conflicts remain. Do not set an arbitrary global missingness cutoff for all clinical variables. Relevance and acceptable completeness depend on the analysis, source design, and documented study requirements. Absence of a non-applicable or unreported optional field is not, by itself, a blocking error. 4. Do not assert a version, license, approval, or source interpretation that cannot be verified. 5. Clinical and sample metadata QC 5.1 Identifiers and record structure Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity ID-01 cohort and identifier availability Nonmissing identifiers required for each table's record grain Error ID-02 Patient keys (cohort, patientid) uniquely identifies patient-level records; repeats are permitted in sample/longitudinal tables Error for invalid grain ID-03 Sample keys (cohort, sampleid) uniquely identifies sample-level records; multiple assays per sample are allowed in an assay-grain table Error for invalid grain ID-04 Patient–sample linkage Each sample resolves to a documented cohort-patient; missing or many-to-many relationships reviewed Error / Review ID-05 Treatment and assessment episodes Distinct treatments/timepoints are not accidentally collapsed or counted as independent patients Review ID-06 Patient attributes across samples Conflicting nonmissing age/sex/disease values are identified and assessed in context of timepoint and record meaning Review Patient counts must be reported using distinct (cohort, patientid) keys . Do not assume patientid is globally unique across cohorts without verified identity linkage. 5.2 Missingness and valid values Assess missingness for every harmonized core variable at its correct grain. Use an explicit denominator: for example, n_missing / n_patients for a patient-level field and n_missing / n_samples for a sample-level field. When cohorts contain longitudinal assessments, report missingness by relevant timepoint/episode rather than only after flattening. Recognize documented missing representations (e.g., blank, NA , N/A , Unknown , Not recorded ), but retain distinguishable missingness reasons where known ( Not assessed , Not reported , Not applicable , Restricted , Unresolved ). An observed negative value is not missing. Where a publication/provider specifies another release, retain the documented source version. Track the source release, genome build, pipeline, and any conversion or feature remapping. Different gene annotations or expression scales are not automatically comparable. For microarrays, retain the source platform, normalization, probe mapping and annotation release; do not describe normalized microarray signals as TPM. Clinical-only cohorts do not need an artificial assay or MAE object. 7. Mapping quality and cross-cohort comparability The dictionary uses Direct , Conditional , Needs review , and Unmapped as mapping statuses. A status describes a mapping decision ; it is not the same as a QC severity or a cohort disposition. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity MAP-01 Source-to-target traceability Source name, original value/code, grain, definition, rule ID and target field retained Error / Review MAP-02 Verified transformations Recode, merge, join, unit conversion or derived value documented and reproducible Error / Review MAP-03 Unresolved mappings Needs review / Unmapped values retained in issue log and excluded from unsupported derived interpretations Review MAP-04 Controlled vocabulary versioning OncoTree, treatment mappings, gene annotation and other resource releases recorded Review MAP-05 Cohort comparability Relevant endpoint definition, treatment context, assay scale, genome build and sampling design assessed for each analysis Review MAP-06 Rule consistency Common transformations have identical versions and semantics across contributing sites Review Cross-cohort comparability should be evaluated for the intended scientific use case . A variable can be syntactically standardized but remain biologically or clinically incomparable; the issue must be visible to analysts. 8. Standard QC reports and output contract Each cohort should generate or document the following artifacts when applicable and permitted . These are recommended names consistent with the SOP ; a shareable aggregate report can be substituted for restricted row-level outputs. <cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Sources, access, versions and authorized paths ├── mapping_log.tsv # Variable-/value-level mapping rules and decisions ├── qc_summary.tsv # One row per QC check, with findings and denominators ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Issue details and decisions, in approved storage ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Assay types and processing/annotation provenance, if present └── run_manifest.txt # Code/environment/input provenance Additional recommended QC views may be produced from the same checks: missingness_summary.tsv , patient_sample_validation.tsv , endpoint_completeness.tsv , and molecular_qc_summary.tsv . Keep one canonical issue log, rather than conflicting copies with different statuses. 8.1 qc_summary.tsv columns Column Meaning cohort Cohort identifier qc_stage Source , Harmonized , Integration , or Release rule_id Stable identifier defined in this document or a versioned rule configuration domain Identity, clinical, outcome, molecular, provenance, mapping, etc. record_grain Cohort, patient, sample, assay, episode, etc. n_checked Number of eligible records checked n_flagged Number of records or instances flagged for this check severity Error , Review , or Info check_status Pass , Flagged , or Not applicable description Concise finding/interpretation issue_log_ref Local pointer to issue record(s), where permitted rule_version QC-rule implementation version run_id Identifier linking the result to the run manifest For rules that apply once per cohort or file, use the appropriate grain and denominator; do not report percentages without explaining the checked population. A flagged finding does not necessarily mean the entire cohort is on hold. 8.2 unresolved_issues.tsv columns Recommended fields: issue_id , cohort , rule_id , affected_grain , affected_record_key (local/restricted where needed), description , severity , mapping_status (if relevant), evidence , proposed_action , owner , reviewer , review_date , resolution , issue_status , run_id . Store patient-level identifiers or sensitive source values only in approved storage. Share sanitized aggregates or non-identifying issue summaries when authorized. 8.3 run_manifest.txt minimum content Record input source IDs and versions/checksums where permitted; workflow/script and Git commit; data dictionary and mapping versions; environment lockfile or package versions; configuration, run date, site/curator, authorized output path, and QC rule version. Re-running against the same permitted inputs and versions should regenerate the QC outputs without manual edits to the final tables. 9. Review and release procedure Execute the applicable QC checks on source, harmonized, and integrated data, as supported by the cohort's modalities. Inspect every Error and clinically material Review finding; document fixes, scientific interpretation, or explicit limitations. Re-run affected checks after code, mapping, or data corrections; preserve the run/version history. Assign a disposition ( Pass , Pass with documented limitations , or Hold for review ) for the specific output and intended analysis. Record the designated reviewer and decision consistent with site responsibilities in the SOP; confirm that sharing and destination are authorized before any cross-site release. Release only approved outputs with their manifests and permissible QC summaries. A held cohort need not be discarded: the relevant issue may affect only a particular assay or endpoint. The release decision should specify what is usable, restricted, pending review, or excluded from a stated analysis. Curation and harmonization QC checklist [ ] Source identity, provenance, access classification and permissions documented. [ ] Required identifiers valid at the correct grain; patient–sample links checked. [ ] Harmonized fields validated against the versioned dictionary. [ ] OncoTree cancer classification and treatment-group mappings reviewed. [ ] Response and OS/PFS definitions, units, event coding and completeness checked. [ ] RNA/DNA assay metadata, GENCODE/source annotation, genome build and processing provenance reviewed where applicable. [ ] SE/MAE and sampleMap validated if created. [ ] Missingness and mapping issues reported with counts, denominators and dispositions. [ ] QC outputs and run manifest saved in approved storage, with the correct version identifiers. [ ] Relevant site reviewer decision and permitted release destination documented. 10. Maintenance and change control The MAR-40 harmonization team maintains this framework alongside the SOP and Data Dictionary . New validation rules must include a stable rule_id , objective, input grain, expected result, severity, implementation version, and examples/test cases. Changes that alter clinical interpretations, mapping categories, endpoint comparability or assay processing require review by the relevant scientific/data leads. Record changes in Git; preserve enough version information to reproduce earlier QC results. If a rule change affects previously released cohorts, assess whether outputs should be regenerated and document that decision. This document defines the QC specification ; executable implementations and configuration are maintained with the workflows described in Usage . docs.text: MAR-40 Usage Guide Version: 1.0 Scope: Participating MAR-40 collaborators at UHN, UCL, and McGill University 1. Purpose This guide explains how collaborators can run the implemented MAR-40 clinical cohort visualization workflow and describes the planned clinical and molecular harmonization examples. It complements the Data Curation SOP , Data Dictionary , Quality Control Framework , and Data Sources Guide . The repository uses Pixi for environment management and Snakemake for the implemented cohort visualization workflow. The proposed clinical/RNA/DNA harmonization pipelines remain separate from this working example and are not yet executable. The workflow must be executable inside each site's approved computing environment. The presence of code or documentation does not authorize the movement of controlled-access or private data between institutions. 2. Two reference examples Two additional planned example cohorts will demonstrate different assay configurations. Neither clinical/molecular harmonization example should be presented as implemented yet. The existing synthetic sample-level dataset is for the implemented descriptive visualization workflow . Example Available inputs Intended outputs Example 1: Clinical + RNA Clinical metadata, RNA expression, patient-to-sample mapping Harmonized clinical metadata and RNA matrix, QC reports, provenance, optional RNA MAE Example 2: Clinical + RNA + DNA Clinical metadata, RNA expression, DNA alteration data, patient-to-sample mapping Harmonized clinical metadata, RNA and DNA data, QC reports, provenance, optional multi-assay MAE Examples should contain synthetic data or data explicitly authorized for public redistribution . They should illustrate realistic source-specific variable names, missing values, and repeated patient samples. They must not contain direct patient identifiers. Assay availability is explicit: Example 1 does not require or generate DNA files. DNA processing is enabled only for cohorts where DNA inputs are declared. 3. Prerequisites and environment Git, to obtain the repository and track code versions. Pixi , to install the locked project environment. Snakemake, R, Python, and Bioconductor dependencies as declared by the project's environment configuration . Read/write permissions for the selected local input and output locations. From a terminal, clone the repository (or use an existing checkout): git clone https://github.com/bhklab/mar40-data-harmonization.git cd mar40-data-harmonization pixi install pixi install assumes the checkout includes a valid Pixi manifest. Do not install additional untracked package versions as a substitute for the agreed project environment; document any site-specific changes. 4. Input data contract For the implemented visualization workflow , the input is a previously harmonized sample-level CSV with required identifiers cohort , patientid , and sampleid . Configure its path in config/visualization.yaml . For the planned molecular examples , provide cohort-specific configurations identifying available clinical and assay inputs. The latter paths below are illustrative and are not assertions that those files exist. data/ ├── examples/ │ └── MAR40_synthetic_sample_level.csv # Existing visualization example ├── rawdata/ │ └── examples/ # Proposed, not yet implemented │ ├── example_clinical_rna/ │ │ ├── clinical.csv │ │ ├── rna_expression.tsv │ │ └── sample_map.csv │ └── example_clinical_rna_dna/ │ ├── clinical.csv │ ├── rna_expression.tsv │ ├── dna_alterations.tsv │ └── sample_map.csv └── procdata/ results/ └── visualization/ └── example/ # Generated outputs 4.1 Clinical metadata The source file should contain a documented patient identifier, and any additional fields available for cancer type, histology, stage, age, sex, treatment, response, survival, and sampling timepoints. The source file does not need to use standardized column names : mappings to the MAR-40 target variables must be documented according to the Data Dictionary . Treat (cohort, patientid) as the unique patient key for cohort-level summaries unless a validated cross-cohort linkage exists. Preserve original source values in the approved environment; do not silently replace unrecognized codes. Document survival units, time origin, and event/censoring conventions before transformation. Missing optional clinical data are reported as missing, not treated as negative observations. 4.2 RNA expression Document whether the input is counts, TPM, another normalized expression scale, or microarray data. Capture the platform, gene identifier system, genome build when relevant, normalization method, transformation, reference annotation release, and sample identifiers. MAR-40 generally uses GENCODE v19 for applicable published/processed datasets and GENCODE v40 for standardized reprocessing when raw data are available ; when a publication or source supplies a specific annotation release, retain that documented information. Do not assume a dataset used GENCODE v19 solely because it is published or its annotation is unknown. Any gene-ID or genome-build conversion must be traceable. 4.3 DNA alterations (Example 2 only) Document the actual assay and input representation (for example, SNV/indel calls, CNA segments, or a curated alteration matrix). Capture the genome build, variant annotation and filtering methods, sample IDs, and rules used to produce a gene-by-sample representation. Do not assume all DNA datasets contain both SNV and CNA data. 4.4 Patient-to-sample linkage A sample mapping file or equivalent verified linkage must associate each assay sample with its clinical patient. Multiple samples per patient and different sample availability across assays are permitted, but ambiguous or unmatched IDs must be reported by QC. 5. Cohort-specific configuration The implemented visualization workflow uses config/visualization.yaml , with a datasets: configuration for harmonized sample-level CSV inputs. The following cohorts: YAML is only a proposal for the future clinical/RNA/DNA workflows ; it is not compatible with the current visualization rules: cohorts: example_clinical_rna: clinical: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna/clinical.csv sample_map: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna/sample_map.csv rna: enabled: true file: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna/rna_expression.tsv units: source_documented annotation: source_documented dna: enabled: false example_clinical_rna_dna: clinical: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/clinical.csv sample_map: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/sample_map.csv rna: enabled: true file: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/rna_expression.tsv units: source_documented annotation: source_documented dna: enabled: true file: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/dna_alterations.tsv representation: source_documented genome_build: source_documented The final schema, mapping-file paths, and workflow target names must match the implemented Snakefile and shared config before execution. 6. Harmonize clinical data: apply versioned source-to-target mappings, controlled values, and unit conversions. Prepare molecular assays: validate identifiers and measurement scales; process RNA and, only where declared, DNA. Validate linkages: check clinical IDs, assay sample IDs, and patient-to-sample relationships. Integrate data: construct appropriate harmonized tables and, where supported, a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE). Run QC: generate missingness, mapping, consistency, assay, and integration checks. Record provenance: capture input versions, code commit, environment, rule versions, exceptions, and output locations. QC checks should flag uncertain mappings rather than silently dropping records. Final release or permitted sharing follows the access conditions and review process defined in the SOP. 7. It does not harmonize source clinical data or process RNA/DNA files. Component Current path Example input data/examples/MAR40_synthetic_sample_level.csv Configuration config/visualization.yaml Workflow entry point workflow/visualization/Snakefile Snakemake rule workflow/visualization/rules.smk Analysis script workflow/visualization/clinical_visualization.R Output directory results/visualization/example/ Execution log logs/visualization/example.log Run the following from the repository root after pixi install : # Check planned jobs without executing them pixi run snakemake --snakefile workflow/visualization/Snakefile --cores 1 --dry-run # Execute the visualization pixi run snakemake --snakefile workflow/visualization/Snakefile --cores 1 # Recheck the workflow after execution pixi run snakemake --snakefile workflow/visualization/Snakefile --cores 1 --dry-run The workflow has been exercised with the synthetic example; Snakemake subsequently reported that its declared outputs were present and up to date. Their harmonization rules, cohort-specific input configurations, QC checks, output contracts, and executable commands will be documented after implementation and testing. Do not run the proposed cohorts: YAML with the current visualization Snakefile . For site-specific use, configure approved local inputs and outputs; do not hard-code personal workstation paths or copy controlled data into Git. 8. Expected output and QC records 8.1 Implemented visualization outputs Outputs from the synthetic example are written to results/visualization/example/ . The declared figures include: 01_cancer_donut.png 02_treatment_donut.png 03_clinical_availability_heatmap.png and 03_clinical_availability_heatmap.pdf 04_sex_by_cohort.png 05_sampling_timing_by_cohort.png 06_recist_by_cohort.png The workflow also produces figure-count CSVs, cohort summaries, variable missingness/availability reports, access summaries, conflict and assay-label reports, observed follow-up summaries, and run_manifest.txt . These descriptive outputs facilitate review but are not substitutes for the full source-level, mapping, endpoint, assay, and release QC defined in the Quality Control Framework . 8.2 Proposed clinical and molecular outputs For each planned cohort example, the target handoff is the following proposed structure, subject to source availability and approved sharing: <approved_output_root>/<cohort_id>/ ├── clinical_harmonized.csv ├── rna_harmonized.* # If RNA data are present ├── dna_harmonized.* # Example 2, if DNA data are present ├── sample_map_validated.csv ├── integrated_mae.rds # Optional, if produced ├── source_manifest.tsv ├── mapping_log.tsv ├── qc_summary.tsv ├── unresolved_issues.tsv └── run_manifest.txt The filenames and exact formats will be finalized with the molecular workflows. Record QC outcomes as Pass , Pass with documented limitations , or Hold for review , as defined in the Quality Control Framework . Cohort-level data availability does not establish analysis readiness. 9. Reproducibility and cross-site collaboration For each run, preserve or reference: Source dataset version and approved location; checksums when allowed. Cohort configuration and applied mapping-rule version. Git commit and Pixi lockfile/environment details. RNA/DNA processing parameters, annotation resources, and software versions. QC results, unresolved mappings, permitted outputs, curator/reviewer information, and execution date. The same workflow should produce structurally comparable outputs at UHN, UCL, and McGill without requiring raw or controlled datasets to cross institutional boundaries. 10. Troubleshooting and implementation status Issue Recommended action Snakemake command not found Confirm pixi install completed, then check pixi run snakemake --version . Pixi dependency installation fails Inspect Python/package compatibility and the errors during environment resolution; document any environment changes. Snakemake cannot find workflow/visualization/Snakefile Run commands from the repository root, or provide the correct --snakefile path. Input CSV not found Check config/visualization.yaml and verify that the input path is accessible locally. R script or package error Inspect logs/visualization/example.log and confirm required R packages in the Pixi environment. Snakemake reports nothing to do Expected when all declared outputs are present and up to date. Unexpected clinical values Check source definitions and the mapping log; flag unsupported mappings rather than inferring values. RNA gene IDs differ across cohorts Verify ID type, source annotation, GENCODE release, and explicit conversion rules (planned molecular examples). Patient/sample IDs fail to join Inspect identifiers, duplicate records, and the verified cohort-patient-sample relationship (planned molecular examples). DNA absent for Clinical + RNA example Expected; the planned configuration sets dna.enabled: false . Restricted input cannot be shared Run locally within an approved environment and share only authorized outputs. Implementation status: The clinical visualization workflow is implemented. Both clinical/RNA/DNA example pipelines are planned; before calling them runnable, provide approved example data, finalize input/output contracts, implement and test Snakemake rules, validate dependencies, and confirm the QC reports produced. docs.text: MAR-40 Cohort Visualization with Snakemake Status: Implemented and validated with a successful Snakemake dry-run. In the latest execution check, the existing visualization outputs were present and up to date; the R script was not rerun. Overview This workflow generates descriptive figures and summary reports from already harmonized, sample-level clinical metadata . It uses R for visualization, Snakemake for workflow orchestration, and Pixi to launch Snakemake. It runs independently of the ICB_Hwang clinical + RNA harmonization workflow. The workflow does not harmonize source data, establish data-access permissions, or confirm that clinical endpoints such as overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) are analysis-ready. Repository structure config/ └── visualization.yaml workflow/ └── visualization/ ├── Snakefile ├── rules.smk └── clinical_visualization.R data/ └── examples/ └── MAR40_synthetic_sample_level.csv results/ └── visualization/ └── <dataset>/ logs/ └── visualization/ └── <dataset>.log The results/ and logs/ directories contain generated outputs and should not be committed to the public repository unless explicitly approved. Input requirements The input is a comma-delimited CSV with one row per sample and the required identifiers: cohort patientid sampleid Additional variables may include cancer type, treatment, sex, age, stage, response, RECIST category, sampling timepoint, OS, PFS, and molecular data availability. Missing values are permitted, including variables unavailable for an entire cohort. Use the MAR-40 Data Dictionary for standardized definitions and accepted values. In particular, distinguish missing values from negative observations and distinguish patient-, sample-, treatment-, and timepoint-level information. Test input: data/examples/MAR40_synthetic_sample_level.csv . This synthetic dataset enables workflow testing without exposing restricted patient-level records. Configuration Dataset inputs are defined in config/visualization.yaml . For example: datasets: example: input: data/examples/MAR40_synthetic_sample_level.csv To process another approved, harmonized dataset, add a named dataset under datasets: with its input CSV path. Each dataset has a separate output directory and log file. If the visualization rule is configured to use a specific R installation, also set the top-level rscript value in config/visualization.yaml and ensure workflow/visualization/rules.smk reads it. docs.text: This workflow generates descriptive figures and summary reports from already harmonized, sample-level clinical metadata . It uses R for visualization, Snakemake for workflow orchestration, and Pixi to launch Snakemake. It runs independently of the ICB_Hwang clinical + RNA harmonization workflow. The workflow does not harmonize source data, establish data-access permissions, or confirm that clinical endpoints such as overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) are analysis-ready.
